<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:small-world_network}
Let $G_n=(V_n,E_n)$ denote $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$, a $d$-dimensional torus with side length $n$, 
and let $\widetilde{G}_n=(V_n,E_n\sqcup \widetilde{E}_n)$ be a random (multi)graph obtained as follows. For each pair $\{x,y\}$ of distinct vertices, let us include the edge $\{x,y\}$ in $\widetilde{E}_n$ with probability $p_{n,x,y}=\frac{Z_n}{|x-y|^r}$, independently, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the graph distance in $G_n$, and $Z_n$ is chosen such that $\sum_{y}p_{n,x,y}=1$ for all $x$. We refer to $\widetilde{G}_n$ as a \emph{small-world network graph}. In what follows, we almost always drop the subscript $n$ from the notation.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:tmix_cutoff}
Let $X$ be a Markov chain on a finite state space $V$, with a unique invariant distribution $\pi$. Then for $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ we define the $\varepsilon$-mixing time of $X$ as
\[
t_{\mathrm{mix}}\left(\varepsilon\right):=\quad\max_{x\in V}\:\inf\left\{t\ge0:\:d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left({\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(X_t=\cdot\right)},{\pi(\cdot)}\right)\le\varepsilon\right\},
\]
where $d_{\mathrm{TV}}$ denotes the total variation distance defined as $d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left({\mu},{\nu}\right)=\frac12\sum_{x}|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|$ for two probability distributions $\mu$, $\nu$ on the same state space.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
We say that a sequence $(A_n)$ of events holds with high probability (whp) if\\ $\mathbb{P}\!\left(A_n\right)=1-o(1)$ as $n\to\infty$. In what follows, the dependence on $n$ will often be suppressed from the notation.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Let $X$ be an irreducible Markov chain with transition matrix $P$. Its absolute relaxation time is defined as $t_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}=\frac{1}{1-\lambda^*}$ where $\lambda^*=\max\{|\lambda|:\:\lambda\ne1\text{ is an eigenvalue of }P\}$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- maintheorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:tmix_trel_order_no_cutoff}
Let $d\ge3$ and consider the small-world graph $\widetilde{G}_n$ as in \Cref{def:small-world_network}, with $r=d$. There exist positive constants $c'$ and $C'$, and for all $\theta\in(0,1)$ there exist positive constants $c(\theta)$ and $C(\theta)$, such that with high probability the following hold.

For all $\theta\in(0,1)$ the mixing time of a simple random walk on $\widetilde{G}_n$ satisfies
\[c(\theta)\log n\quad\le\quadt_{\mathrm{mix}}\left(\theta\right)\quad\le\quad C(\theta)\log n,\]
and the absolute relaxation time of a simple random walk on $\widetilde{G}_n$ satisfies
\[c'\log n\quad\le\quadt_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\quad\le\quad C'\log n.\]
<!-- end maintheorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
For the lazy random walk on $\widetilde{G}_n$, i.e.\ the Markov chain with transition matrix $\frac12(I+P)$ where $P$ is the transition matrix of a simple random walk on $\widetilde{G}_n$, the results of \Cref{thm:tmix_trel_order_no_cutoff} also hold. We see this by combining Lemmas~\ref{tmixlazy_upper_bound}, \ref{trelabs_lower_bound} and \ref{trel_asymp_trelabs}.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
In \Cref{thm:tmix_trel_order_no_cutoff} we establish that with high probability the mixing time and the absolute relaxation time of the walk on $\widetilde{G}_n$ are of the same order, hence by \cite[Proposition 18.4]{MTMC} with high probability there is no cutoff. This means that there exist $c>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that with high probability $\frac{t_{\mathrm{mix}}\left(\varepsilon\right)}{t_{\mathrm{mix}}\left(1-\varepsilon\right)}\ge1+c$.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
We emphasise that the constants in \Cref{thm:tmix_trel_order_no_cutoff} depend on the dimension $d$. We believe that $t_{\mathrm{mix}}\asymp d^2\log n$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:Gstar}
We construct a random graph $G^*$ as follows. We start from the torus $G$, and say that its edges are black. Then for each $x$ and $y$ in $G$ with probability $p^{\mathrm{blue}}_{x,y}$ we add a blue edge between them. Then for each $x$ and $y$ with probability $p^{\mathrm{green}}_{x,y}$ we add a green edge between them, and finally for each $x$ and $y$ with probability $p^{\mathrm{red}}_{x,y}$ add a red edge between them. The presence or lack of these edges are all chosen independently from each other.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{couple_Gtil_Gstar}
There exists a coupling of $G^*$ and $\widetilde{G}$ such that the two graphs agree with probability $1-O\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For each pair $\{x,y\}$ the probability that the optimal coupling between the added edges between them in $\widetilde{G}$ and $G^*$ fails is $2p^{\mathrm{blue}}_{x,y}\left(p^{\mathrm{green}}_{x,y}+p^{\mathrm{red}}_{x,y}\right)\asympp^{\mathrm{blue}}\cdot p_{x,y}$.

Let us use the optimal coupling for each $\{x,y\}$, independently for different pairs. Then the probability that at least one of these optimal couplings fails is $\lesssimp^{\mathrm{blue}}\sum_{x,y}p_{x,y}\asymp\frac{1}{N\log N}N\asymp\frac{1}{\log N}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:hit_time}
Let $X$ be a Markov chain on a finite state space $V$ with a unique invariant distribution $\pi$. For each $\alpha,\theta\in(0,1)$ we define the corresponding \emph{hit time} of $X$ as
\[
\mathrm{hit}_{\alpha}\left(\theta\right):=\quad\inf\{t:\:\forall x,\:\forall A\subseteq V\text{ with }\pi(A)\ge\alpha\text{ we have }\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_A>t\right)\le\theta\},
\]
where $\tau_A=\inf\left\{t:\:X_t\in A\right\}$.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{hit_upper_bound}
For any $\theta,\alpha\in(0,1)$ there exists a positive constant $C$ such that whp the graph $G^*$ has the following property. The hit time of a simple random walk on $G^*$ with parameters $\alpha$ and $\theta$ satisfies $\mathrm{hit}_{\alpha}\left(\theta\right)\le C\log N$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{tmixlazy_upper_bound}
There exists a positive constant $C$ such that whp $G^*$ satisfies the following. The mixing time of a lazy random walk on $G^*$ can be upper bounded as $t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{\mathrm{lazy}}\le C\log N$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{trelabs_lower_bound}
There exists a positive constant $C$ such that whp the Cheeger constant of $G^*$ satisfies $\Phi^*\le\frac{C}{\log N}$. From this, it follows that there is a positive constant $c$ such that whp the absolute relaxation time of a simple random walk on $G^*$ satisfies $t_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\ge c\log N$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{trel_asymp_trelabs}
There exist positive constants $c$ and $C$ such that whp $G^*$ has the following property. The relaxation time and the absolute relaxation time of a simple random walk on $G^*$ satisfy $ct_\mathrm{rel}\let_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\le Ct_\mathrm{rel}$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
First let us prove the results for the modified graph $G^*$.

From \Cref{tmixlazy_upper_bound} we know that $t_\mathrm{rel}\lesssimt_{\mathrm{mix}}^{\mathrm{lazy}}\lesssim\log N$ whp, from \Cref{trelabs_lower_bound} we know that $t_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\gtrsim\log N$ whp and from \Cref{trel_asymp_trelabs} we know that $t_\mathrm{rel}\asympt_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ whp. Together, these give that whp $t_\mathrm{rel}\asympt_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\asymp\log N$.

Using this, \Cref{hit_upper_bound} and~\cite[Proposition 1.8 and Remark 1.9]{characterisation_of_cutoff} we get that whp $t_{\mathrm{mix}}\left(\theta\right)\asympt_{\mathrm{mix}}^{\mathrm{lazy}}\left(\theta\right)\asymp\log N$ for all $\theta\in(0,1)$.

Since $t_{\mathrm{mix}}\asympt_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}$ and $t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{\mathrm{lazy}}\asympt_\mathrm{rel}$, neither a simple nor a lazy random walk exhibits cutoff.

From \Cref{couple_Gtil_Gstar} we know that $G^*$ and $\widetilde{G}$ can be coupled to agree whp, hence the results also carry over to $\widetilde{G}$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{tauhat_transition_probs}
There exist positive constants $\theta$ and $C$ such that whp $G^*$ satisfies the following. There exists a random time $\tau$ such that $\tau\le C\log N$, and for any $x,y\in V$, we have $\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(X_{\tau}=y\;\middle\vert\;G^*\right)\ge\theta\frac{\deg(y)}{N}$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{max_deg}
There exists a constant $C$ such that with probability $1-o\left(\frac1N\right)$ all vertices $v$ in $G^*$ satisfy $\deg(v)\le C\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}=:d_{\mathrm{max}}$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
For each $v$ we upper bound $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\deg(v)\ge C\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}\right)$ using \Cref{sum_of_Berns} and get that for sufficiently large $C$ this is $\ll\frac{1}{N^2}$. Then we take a union bound over $v$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{total_degree}
Whp the sum of all green, red and blue degrees in $G^*$ satisfies $N-N^{\frac23}\le\sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{rgb}}(v)\le N+N^{\frac23}$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Note that $\frac12\sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{rgb}}(v)=\sum_{\{x,y\}:x\ne y}\left(\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{g}} y}+\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{r}} y}+\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} y}\right)$ is a sum of independent Bernoulli random variables and has mean $\frac12N$. Then use for example, \Cref{sum_indep_RVs}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{total_blue_degree}
Whp the sum of all blue degrees in $G^*$ satisfies $c_{\mathrm{b}}\frac{N}{\log N}-\sqrt{N}\le\sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\le c_{\mathrm{b}}\frac{N}{\log N}+\sqrt{N}$ where $c_{\mathrm{b}}\asymp1$ is such that $p^{\mathrm{blue}}=\frac{c_{\mathrm{b}}}{N\log N}$. Also, $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\ge2c_{\mathrm{b}}\frac{N}{\log N}\right)\ll\frac{1}{N^2}$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Note that $\frac12\sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)=\sum_{\{x,y\}:x\ne y}\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} y}$ is a sum of independent $\mathrm{Bern}\!\left(p^{\mathrm{blue}}\right)$ random variables, and use e.g.\ \Cref{sum_indep_RVs}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{volume_tail_bound}
For any radius $r$, any $s>0$ and any given vertex $x$ of $G^*$, the volume of a ball $B_r$ of radius $r$ centred at $x$ can be bounded as
\[\mathbb{P}\!\left(|B_r|\ge(2d+3)^rs\right)\quad\le\quad e^{\frac14}e^{-\frac14s}.\]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{volume_high_prob_bound}
For any constant $C'>0$ there exists a constant $C$ such that for any $r\ge C'\log\log N$ whp every ball of radius $r$ in $G^*$ has volume $\le e^{Cr}$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:random_quasi_tree}
A \emph{random quasi-tree} is a random graph $T$ together with a map $\iota$ from its vertices to the vertex set of $G$, obtained as follows.

We start from a root vertex $\rho$ with some associated $\iota(\rho)$. Then we consider a ball of radius $R$ around $\iota(\rho)$ in a random copy of $G_{\mathrm{g}}$, and for each vertex in this ball we also add its neighbourhood of radius $R$ in $G$. We call the resulting neighbourhood of $\rho$ an \emph{$(R+R)$-ball}, and for each vertex $v$ in it we let $\iota(v)$ be the corresponding vertex in $G$.

{Then for each vertex $v$ in the $(R+R)$-ball, we sample $d_{\mathrm{r}}(v)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}d_{\mathrm{r}}$ independently, and add this many new edges from it, called \emph{long-range edges}.}
For each $w$ that is the new endpoint of a newly added long-range edge from a vertex $v$, we sample $\iota(w)$ choosing a vertex $x$ with probability proportional to $p^{\mathrm{red}}_{\iota(v),x}$, and attach a new $(R+R)$-ball around it, sampling from a new copy of $G_{\mathrm{g}}$. {Then we continue analogously from each new $(R+R)$-ball.}

The copies of $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ we use for the different $(R+R)$-balls, the long-range degrees $d_{\mathrm{r}}(v)$ of the vertices, and the choices of $\iota$ for the new endpoints of the long-range edges are all independent.

For simplicity, we sometimes refer to an $(R+R)$-ball as a \emph{ball}.

We call the set of vertices in an $(R+R)$-ball that are of graph distance $\ge R$ from its centre the \emph{boundary} of the ball. We use the graph distance of the quasi-tree $T$. (Note that this is different from the usual definition of a boundary.)
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{def:quasi-tree_of_Gstar}
{Given the graph $G^*$ and a vertex $x$ of $G^*$, the \emph{quasi-tree from $x$ associated to $G^*$} is a graph $T_x(G^*)$ together with a map $\iota$ from its vertices to the vertex set of $G$, obtained as follows.}

{We start from a root vertex $\rho$ with $\iota(\rho)=x$.} Then we consider a ball of radius $R$ around $\iota(\rho)$ in $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ and for each vertex in this ball we also add its neighbourhood of radius $R$ in $G$. We call the resulting neighbourhood of $\rho$ an $(R+R)$-ball, and for each vertex $v$ in it we let $\iota(v)$ be the corresponding vertex in $G$.

Then for each vertex $v$ in the $(R+R)$-ball, including the centre, we add $d_{\mathrm{r}}(\iota(v))$ new edges from it, called long-range edges, and we let $\iota$ map the new endpoints of those edges to the red neighbours of $\iota(v)$. For each new endpoint $w$ we attach an $(R+R)$-ball around it according to the neighbourhood of $\iota(w)$ in $G_{\mathrm{g}}$, and for each vertex $u$ in this $(R+R)$-ball we add a number of long-range edges from $u$ so that the total number of long-range edges from $u$ is $d_{\mathrm{r}}(\iota(u))$. We continue similarly with the new endpoints of these long-range edges.

We call the set of vertices in an $(R+R)$-ball that are of graph distance $\ge R$ from its centre the boundary of the ball.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
\label{def:quasi-tree_notation}
For vertices $x$ and $y$ in a quasi-tree $T$, their \emph{long-range distance} $d_T(x,y)$ is the minimal number of long-range edges a path from $x$ to $y$ has to cross. The \emph{level} of a vertex $x$ is its long-range distance from the root, and it is denoted by $\ell(x)$. Note that all vertices within a ball have the same level, we also refer to this as the level of the ball. For a long-range edge $e=\{x,y\}$ we define its level $\ell(e)$ as $\ell(x)\vee\ell(y)$, and we denote its two endpoints by $e^+$ and $e^-$ such that $\ell(e^+)=\ell(e)$. For a vertex $x$ in $T$, we write $T(x)$ for the quasi-tree obtained by removing the long-range edge that leads to the ball of $x$ from a smaller level (if there is one) and keeping the connected component of~$x$. We say that a long-range edge $e$ is a \emph{descendant} of a long-range edge $f$ in $T$ if every path between $e^+$ and the root of $T$ crosses $f$. We say that $e$ is an \emph{ancestor} of $f$ if $f$ is a descendant of $e$. We use analogous terminology for balls in $T$.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{def:binary_RplusR_ball}
We say that an $(R+R)$-ball is \emph{binary} if it has the following property. For each of its vertices $v$, there is a copy of $\left[0,\frac1dR\right]^d$ in the $(R+R)$-ball that contains $v$ and has at least 3 long-range edges emanating from it (including any edges emanating from $v$). Here $\left[0,\frac1dR\right]^d$ denotes a $d$-dimensional box of side length $\frac1dR$, with edges induced by $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{transience_in_binary_tree}
There exists a constant $p_{\mathrm{esc}}\in(0,1)$ ({not depending on $C_R$ or any parameter other than possibly $d$}) with the following property. Let $T$ be a realisation of a random quasi-tree where each $(R+R)$-ball is binary in the sense of \Cref{def:binary_RplusR_ball}, and let $v$ be a vertex in $T$. Then starting a simple random walk on $T$ from $v$, with probability at least $\frac{p_{\mathrm{esc}}}{\deg_T(v)}$ the walk never returns to $v$.

Moreover, if $(v,w)$ is a long-range edge of $T$, then starting a simple random walk on $T$ from $v$, with probability at least $\frac{p_{\mathrm{esc}}}{\deg_T(v)}$ the walk never returns to $v$ or hits $w$ {and with probability at least $p_{\mathrm{esc}}$ the walk never hits $w$}.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{transience_until_nonbinary}
Let $T$ be any realisation of a random quasi-tree and let $v$ be a vertex of $T$. Let $p_{\mathrm{esc}}\in(0,1)$ be as in Lemma~\ref{transience_in_binary_tree}. Then
\begin{align*}
{\mathbb{P}_{v}\!\left(\tau_v^+>\tau_{\mathrm{non-bin}}\;\middle\vert\;T\right)\quad\ge\quad\frac{p_{\mathrm{esc}}}{\deg_T(v)}},
\end{align*}
where $\tau_{\mathrm{non-bin}}$ denotes the first time that $X$ hits a non-binary $(R+R)$-ball {and $\tau_v^+=\inf\{t>0: X_t=v\}$ is the first time the walk returns to $v$}.

Moreover, if $(v,w)$ is a long-range edge of $T$, then
\begin{align*}
{\mathbb{P}_{v}\!\left(\tau_v^+\wedge\tau_w>\tau_{\mathrm{non-bin}}\;\middle\vert\;T\right)\quad\ge\quad\frac{p_{\mathrm{esc}}}{\deg_T(v)} \quad \text{and}\quad \mathbb{P}_{v}\!\left(\tau_w>\tau_{\mathrm{non-bin}}\;\middle\vert\;T\right)\quad\ge\quadp_{\mathrm{esc}}}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
It is sufficient to prove the second part of the claim, as it also implies the first one.

From~\cite[Theorem 2.11]{prob-on-trees-and-networks} we know that a SRW on a graph is transient if and only if there is a unit flow of finite energy from some vertex of the graph to $\infty$.

Let $T_{-w}$ be obtained from $T$ by removing the edge $(v,w)$ and only keeping the connected component of $v$. We will construct a unit flow {$\theta$ from $v$ to $\infty$ on $T_{-w}$ of energy bounded by constant}. This shows that a SRW on $T_{-w}$, starting from $v$, has at least {$\frac{\rm{const}}{\deg_T(v)-1}$ probability of never returning to $v$. Then the probability that a SRW on $T$ from $v$ does not pass through $(v,w)$ in the first step and never returns to $v$ is also at least $\frac{\rm{const}}{\deg_T(v)-1}$. Further, on every visit to $v$ the walk has probability $\frac{1}{\deg_T(v)}$ to pass through $(v,w)$, giving the constant lower bound on the probability to never pass through $w$. We set $p_{\mathrm{esc}}$ to be the smallest of these constants.}

In $T_{-w}$ let $\left(e^0_1\right)^+=v$, let $e^{1}_1$ and $e^{1}_2$ be two long-range edges from a box of side length $\frac1dR$ containing $v$, and for $k=1,2,...$ and $j\in\{1,2,...,2^k\}$ let $e^{k+1}_{2j-1}$ and $e^{k+1}_{2j}$ be two long-range edges (other than $e^{k}_{j}$) from a box of side length $\frac1dR$ containing $\left(e^{k}_{j}\right)^+$. From \Cref{unit_flow_in_box} we know that there exist unit flows $\theta^{k+1}_{2j-1}$ and $\theta^{k+1}_{2j}$ in the $(R+R)$-ball of $\left(e^{k}_{j}\right)^+$, from $\left(e^{k}_{j}\right)^+$ to $\left(e^{k+1}_{2j-1}\right)^-$ and $\left(e^{k+1}_{2j}\right)^-$, respectively with energies bounded by a constant $C$.

Let $\theta$ be a unit flow from $v$ to $\infty$ constructed by considering $\sum_{k\ge0}\sum_{j=1}^{2^k}2^{-k}\theta^k_j$ and also adding a flow of strength $2^{-k}$ along each $e^k_j$. Then $\theta$ has energy $\le\sum_{k\ge0}2^k\cdot \left(2^{-2k}\cdot4C\right)+\sum_{k\ge0}2^k\cdot2^{-2k}\lesssim 1$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{transience_until_boundary}
There exists a positive constant $c$ with the following property.

For any realisation $T$ of a random quasi-tree, and any vertex $x$ of $T$, we have
\[
\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\quad\ge\quad\frac{c}{\deg_T(x)},
\]
while for any long-range edge $e$, we have
\[
\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_e>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\quad\ge\quad c.
\]
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Firstly, we note that for any realisation of $T$ we have $\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}=\infty\right)=0$, so in the following calculations we can use events like $\{\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\}$ and $\{\tau_x^+\ge\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\}$ interchangeably.

Once we establish the first inequality, the second one follows by noting that it is sufficient to consider the case when $x$ is one of the endpoints of $e$, using that in this case \[\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_e<\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\quad=\quad\frac{1}{\deg_T(x)}\sum_{k\ge0}\left(1-\frac{1}{\deg_T(x)}\right)^k\mathbb{P}_{x}^{T\setminus\{e\}}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)^k,\] and using the first inequality for $T\setminus\{e\}$. We present the proof of the first inequality below.

Let $X$ be a simple random walk on $T$ started from $x$ and let $Y$ be a simple random walk on the $(R+R)$-ball of $x$, started from $x$, coupled to $X$ such that it agrees with the restriction of $X$ to the $(R+R)$-ball of $x$ as long as the latter one is defined. \footnote{By the restriction of $X$ to the $(R+R)$-ball we mean a (possibly finite) walk obtained by removing the steps of $X$ taken outside this ball, and then from the remaining walk removing the steps where it stays in place. Note that after $X$ exits the ball, it can only return to it via the same edge, hence the restriction of $X$ to the ball is a simple random walk on the ball, with a random killing time.} Note that if $X$ does not cross a long-range edge in the first step, and $Y$ does not return to $x$ without hitting a boundary first, then $X$ does not return to $x$ without hitting a boundary first either. Hence we can write
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\:\ge&\:\frac{\deg_T(x)-d_{\mathrm{r}}(x)}{\deg_T(x)}\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\;\middle\vert\;\text{first step within the }(R+R)\text{-ball of }x\right)\\
\ge&\:\frac{\deg_T(x)-d_{\mathrm{r}}(x)}{\deg_T(x)}\mathbb{P}_{x}^{Y}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right),
\end{align*}
where $d_{\mathrm{r}}(x)$ denotes the number of long-range edges from $x$ in $T$. So it is sufficient to show that $\mathbb{P}_{x}^{Y}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\gtrsim\frac{1}{\deg_T(x)-d_{\mathrm{r}}(x)}$.

Let us consider a realisation of $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ such that the $(R+R)$-ball of $x$ in $T$ is isomorphic to the corresponding neighbourhood of $x$ in $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ and let $Z$ be a simple random walk on $G_{\mathrm{g}}$, started from $x$. Note that $Z$ can be coupled to $Y$ so that they agree until $\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}$. Let $B$ be a ball of radius $\frac14n$ around $x$ in $G_{\mathrm{g}}$, according to the torus graph distance. Since $R\cdot D^{1-\beta}+R<\frac14n$, we have
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}_{x}^{Y}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\quad=\quad\mathbb{P}_{x}^{Z}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{boundary}}\right)\quad\ge\quad\mathbb{P}_{x}^{Z}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{B^c}\right),
\end{align*}
where $\tau_{B^c}$ denotes the first time that $Z$ exits the ball $B$.

Viewing $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ as an electric network, we see that $\mathbb{P}_{x}^{Z}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{B^c}\right)=\frac{1}{\deg_{G_{\mathrm{g}}}(x)R_{\mathrm{eff}}^{G_{\mathrm{g}}}\left(x,\:B^c\right)}$, so it is sufficient to show that $R_{\mathrm{eff}}^{G_{\mathrm{g}}}\left(x,\:B^c\right)\lesssim1$. By Rayleigh's monotonicity principle, it is sufficient to show that $R_{\mathrm{eff}}^{G}\left(x,\:B^c\right)\lesssim1$, which follows by noting that the restriction of the torus $G$ to the ball $B$ is isomorphic to a ball in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and using the transience of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq 3$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{def:atypical_ball}
We say that an $(R+R)$-ball in a quasi-tree $T$ is \emph{atypical} if any of the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item\label{item:nonbinary} It is not binary in the sense of \Cref{def:binary_RplusR_ball}.
\item\label{item:large_deg} It contains a vertex with degree larger than $d_{\mathrm{max}}$. (Here $d_{\mathrm{max}}$ is defined as in \Cref{max_deg}).
\item\label{item:hit_boundary}
{It satisfies that $p_\partial >\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^5$ where $p_\partial$ is defined as follows. Let $Y$ be a walk starting from the centre of the $(R+R)$-ball, which evolves like a simple random walk except for the following. Every time it crosses a long-range edge from the ball, with probability $p_{\mathrm{esc}}$ it gets terminated, otherwise, it crosses the long-range edge back and continues. Let $p_\partial$ be the probability of $Y$ visiting at least $R$ different vertices before getting terminated. (Here $p_{\mathrm{esc}}$ is the constant from \Cref{transience_in_binary_tree}.)}
\item\label{item:large_vol} It contains more than $e^{C_{\mathrm{vol}} R}$ vertices. (Here $C_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is a sufficiently large constant, to be specified later.)
\end{enumerate}
Otherwise we say that the $(R+R)$-ball is \emph{typical}.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rmk:atypical_ball}
Note that the event that a given $(R+R)$-ball is atypical only depends on the ball itself and the red degrees of its vertices, but not on the rest of the quasi-tree. Point \eqref{item:hit_boundary} is formulated as it is to ensure this property.

Note that by~\eqref{item:hit_boundary} and~\Cref{transience_until_nonbinary}, a walk starting from the centre of a typical $(R+R)$-ball has probability $\le\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^5$ of visiting $\ge R$ different vertices in this ball without encountering a non-binary $(R+R)$-ball first.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
\label{def:typical_events}
For a given quasi-tree $T$, a walk $X$ on it and (possibly random) times $k_1$ and $k_2$ we say that the event $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(k_1,k_2\right)$ holds if during the time interval $[k_1,k_2]$ the walk $X$ does not visit an atypical $(R+R)$-ball. We write $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(k\right)$ to mean $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(0,k\right)$.

We say that $\Omega_{\partial}\left(k_1,k_2\right)$ holds if there is no $(R+R)$-ball where the walk $X$ visits $\ge R= C_R\log\log N$ different vertices in time interval $[k_1,k_2]$. We also write $\Omega_{\partial}\left(k\right)$ to mean $\Omega_{\partial}\left(0,k\right)$.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{bound_atyp_prob}
For any positive constant $b$, there exists a positive constant $C$ such that for sufficiently large values of $C_R$ the following holds. For a randomly sampled $(R+R)$-ball, the probability that it is atypical in the sense of \Cref{def:atypical_ball} is $\le C\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^b$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{T_volume_tail_bound}
For any radius $r$, any $s>0$, the volume of a ball $B_r$ of radius $r$ around the root of a random quasi-tree (in the graph distance of the quasi-tree) can be bounded as
\[\mathbb{P}\!\left(|B_r|\ge(2d+3)^rs\right)\quad\le\quad e^{\frac14}e^{-\frac14s}.\]
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{small_vol_implies_likely_binary}
There exists $c>0$ with the following property. For a randomly sampled $(R+R)$-ball, the probability that it has volume $\le e^{C_{\mathrm{vol}} R}$, but is not binary, is $\lesssim e^{-cR^d}$.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{bound_range_in_ball_until_tauatyp}
There exist positive constants $c_1$, $c_2$ and $c_3$ (with $c_1$ and $c_2$ depending on $d$, and $c_3$ depending on $d$ and $\beta$), and a sequence $(p_k)_{k\ge1}$ in $(0,1)$ satisfying $p_k\ge c_1\wedge\frac{c_2\log\log N}{k}$ for all $k\le N^{c_3}$, such that the following holds.

Let us consider a copy of $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ and for each of its vertices $v$, let us attach $d_{\mathrm{r}}(v)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}d_{\mathrm{r}}$  red edges to it, independently of each other and everything else. Then let us consider a walk $Y$ that takes steps like a simple random walk except for the following. Every time it crosses a red edge, with probability $p_{\mathrm{esc}}$ it gets terminated, otherwise it crosses the red edge back and continues.

Then we have
\[|R^{Y}\cap V_{\mathrm{g}}|\1{\Omega_\mathrm{deg}}\quad\le_{\mathrm{st}}\quad \mathrm{GGeom}_{\ge1}\left((p_k)\right),\]
where $R^{Y}$ denotes the range of $Y$ (up to the time it gets terminated), $V_{\mathrm{g}}$ denotes the set of vertices in the copy of $G_{\mathrm{g}}$ (i.e.\ the new endpoints of the added red edges are not included), and $\Omega_\mathrm{deg}$ denotes the event that $Y$ does not visit any vertex of degree $>d_{\mathrm{max}}$ until it gets terminated.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By \Cref{max_deg} the probability that \eqref{item:large_deg} holds is $\ll\frac1N$, and by\\ \Cref{T_volume_tail_bound} the probability that \eqref{item:large_vol} holds is also $\ll\frac1N$ for sufficiently large $C_{\mathrm{vol}}$.

By \Cref{small_vol_implies_likely_binary} the probability that \eqref{item:nonbinary} holds, but \eqref{item:large_vol} does not hold is $\lesssim e^{-cR^d}\ll\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^b$ for any $b>0$.

By \Cref{bound_range_in_ball_until_tauatyp} the probability that \eqref{item:hit_boundary} holds, but \eqref{item:large_deg} does not can be bounded as
\begin{align*}
\le\quad\mathbb{P}\!\left(\mathrm{GGeom}_{\ge1}\left((p_k)\right)\ge R\right)\quad=\quad\prod_{k=1}^{R-1}(1-p_k)\quad&\le\quad \prod_{k=\frac{c_2}{c_1}\log\log N}^{C_R\log\log N-1}\left(1-\frac{c_2\log\log N}{k}\right)\\
&\le\quad\exp\left(-\sum_{k=\frac{c_2}{c_1}\log\log N}^{(C_R-1)\log\log N}\frac{c_2\log\log N}{k}\right),
\end{align*}
where for the second inequality we assumed that $C_R>\frac{c_2}{c_1}$. Note that for given positive constants $c_1$ and $c_2$, the sum $\sum_{k=\frac{c_2}{c_1}\log\log N}^{(C_R-1)\log\log N}\frac{c_2}{k}$ can be made arbitrarily large by choosing the constant $C_R$ sufficiently large. This finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Assume that the volume of the $(R+R)$-ball is $\le e^{C_{\mathrm{vol}} R}$.
Let $(\Lambda_i)_{i\in I}$ be a collection of copies of $\left[0,\frac1dR\right]^d$ in the $(R+R)$-ball that cover all vertices of the ball, such that $|I|\le e^{C_{\mathrm{vol}} R}$. For each $\Lambda_i$, the probability that there are at most 2 red edges coming out of it is $\lesssim R^{2d}e^{-aR^d}$ where $a$ is a positive constant. The probability that at least one of the $\Lambda_i$ has this property is $\lesssim e^{C_{\mathrm{vol}} R}R^{2d}e^{-aR^d}\lesssim e^{-cR^d}$ for some positive constant $c$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
For the purposes of the proof we consider a walk $Z$ that takes steps like $Y$, except that it can only get terminated when it crosses a red edge from a vertex in $V_{\mathrm{g}}$ it visited for the first time. It is clear that $Y$ and $Z$ can be coupled such that $Y$ gets terminated no later than $Z$ and they agree up to this time. Hence for any $k$ we have $\mathbb{P}\!\left(|R^Y\capV_{\mathrm{g}}|\1{\Omega_\mathrm{deg}}\ge k\right)\le\mathbb{P}\!\left(|R^Z\capV_{\mathrm{g}}|\ge k,\:\Omega^Z_\mathrm{deg}(k)\right)$ where $R^Z$ denotes the range of $Z$ and $\Omega^Z_\mathrm{deg}(k)$ is the event that the first $k$ different vertices visited by $Z$ (or all different vertices visited by $Z$ if it gets terminated earlier) have degree $\led_{\mathrm{max}}$.

Let us explore the random graph (call it $H$) as we proceed with the walk $Z$. Let $v_0=Z_0$. Whenever we encounter a new vertex $x$, we reveal $d_{\mathrm{r}}(x)$ and $d_{\mathrm{g}}(x)$. When $Z$ crosses a red or green edge for the first time, we also reveal the other endpoint of that edge. We will denote the $k$-th new vertex in $V_{\mathrm{g}}$ that $Z$ visits by $v_k$, and the $\sigma$-algebra generated by everything we know up to then by $\mathcal{F}_k$. Let $c_3$ be the constant from \Cref{cond_green_red_deg}. For $k>N^{c_3}$ let $p_k=0$. For $k=1,2,..., N^{c_3}$ we do the following in the $k$th round.

(A) Description of the exploration:

We start the $k$th round by revealing the green and red degree of $v_{k-1}$. (The distribution of the green degree depends on $\mathcal{F}_{k-1}$.)

Let $A_k$ be the event that the walk in the next step crosses a red edge from $v_{k-1}$ and gets terminated. Note that by definition $\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(A_k\;\middle\vert\;H\right)=\frac{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k-1})}{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k-1})+d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k-1})+2d}\cdotp_{\mathrm{esc}}$, hence $\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(A_k\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k-1}\right)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k-1})}{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k-1})+d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k-1})+2d}\cdotp_{\mathrm{esc}}\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k-1}\right]$, and that on this event we have $|R^Z\capV_{\mathrm{g}}|\le k+1$.

In case $A_k$ does not hold, we proceed with the exploration as follows. With probability $\frac{2d}{d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k-1})+2d}$ we let the walk cross a uniformly chosen black edge from $v_{k-1}$. With probability $\frac{d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k-1})}{d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k-1})+2d}$ the walk crosses a uniformly chosen green edge from $v_{k-1}$. We know what the distribution of the other endpoint of a uniformly chosen green edge from $v_{k-1}$ is, so we sample a vertex according to that and let the walk step there. (Note that this distribution depends on what we have explored so far.)

If the step leads the walk to a yet unvisited vertex, then we call that vertex $v_k$. Otherwise we keep taking steps until the walk visits a new vertex, and we call that vertex $v_k$. We denote the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the exploration up to visiting the $k$th new vertex $v_k$ by $\mathcal{F}_k$.

(B) Estimates on the degrees:

We will define a sequence $(p_k)_{k=0}^{N^{c_3}}$ of constants such that for each $k$ we have $p_k\asymp 1\wedge\frac{\log\log N}{k}$ and $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})}{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})+d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k})+2d}\cdotp_{\mathrm{esc}}\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k}\right]\ge p_k$.

We know that $\mathbb{P}\!\left(d_{\mathrm{r}}\ge1\right)$ is bounded away from 0, say it is lower bounded by a constant $q\in(0,1)$. In what follows, let us work conditional on $\mathcal{F}_{k}$ and assume that none of $v_0,...,v_{k-1}$ has green degree larger than $d_{\mathrm{max}}$.

Let $\ell\in\{0,2,...,k-1\}$ be such that the walk first visited $v_k$ by crossing an edge from $v_{\ell}$ to $v_k$. Then we know that there is a green or black edge running between $v_{\ell}$ and $v_{k}$. Using \eqref{eq:simg_cond_prob} from \Cref{cond_green_red_deg}, we can bound the number of green connections between $v_k$ and $\{v_0,...,v_{k-1}\}\setminus\{v_{\ell}\}$ as 
\[
\left(\1{v_{j}\sim_{\mathrm{g}} v_{k}}\right)_{j\in\{0,1,...,k-1\}\setminus\{\ell\}}\quad\le_{\mathrm{st}}\quad \left(\mathrm{Bern}\!\left(cd_{\mathrm{g}}(v_j)p^{\mathrm{green}}_{v_j,v_k}\right)\right)_{j\in\{0,1,...,k-1\}\setminus\{\ell\}},
\]
where $c$ is a positive constant, and the Bernoulli random variables are independent. \footnote{Consider the $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{G}_k$ generated by $\mathcal{F}_k$ and by revealing all green edges running between the vertices $v_0,...,v_{k-1}$. Then conditional on $\mathcal{G}_k$, for each $j\in\{0,1,...,k-1\}\setminus\{\ell\}$, the vertex $v_j$ has $d_{\mathrm{g}}'(v_j)\led_{\mathrm{g}}(v_j)$ green half-edges that are not yet matched, and the only information we have about their other endpoints is that they do not lie in $\{v_0,...,v_{k-1}\}$. Conditional on $\mathcal{G}_k$, the events $\{v_j\sim_{\mathrm{g}} v_k\}$ are independent for the different $j\in\{0,1,...,k-1\}\setminus\{\ell\}$ and $\mathbb{P}\left(v_j\sim_{\mathrm{g}} v_k\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{G}_k\right)=\mathbb{P}\left(v_j\sim_{\mathrm{g}} v_k\;\middle\vert\;d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_j)=d_{\mathrm{g}}'(v_j),v_j\not\sim_{\mathrm{g}} v_i\text{ for }i\in\{0,1,...,k-1\} \right)$. Using \eqref{eq:simg_cond_prob} and that $k\le N^{c_3}$ we see that this probability is $\lesssimd_{\mathrm{g}}'(v_j)p^{\mathrm{green}}_{v_j,v_k}\led_{\mathrm{g}}(v_j)p^{\mathrm{green}}_{v_j,v_k}$.}

On the event we are working on, we have $d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_j)p^{\mathrm{green}}_{v_j,v_k}\led_{\mathrm{max}}\cdotp^{\mathrm{green}}_{\max}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}\cdot\frac{1}{\log N}$, hence the above random variable is
\[
\le_{\mathrm{st}}\quad\left(\mathrm{Bern}\!\left(\frac{\widetilde{C}}{\log\log N}\right)\right)_{j\in\{0,1,...,k-2\}}
\]
where $\widetilde{C}$ is a positive constant, and the Bernoulli random variables are independent.

For any $v\not\in\{v_0,...,v_k\}$, we have $\1{v\sim_{\mathrm{g}} v_k}\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}\mathrm{Bern}\!\left(p^{\mathrm{green}}_{v,v_k}\right)$, independently of anything else. Hence
\[
d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k})\quad\le_{\mathrm{st}}\quad 1+\mathrm{Bin}\!\left(k-1,\frac{\widetilde{C}}{\log\log N}\right)+d_{\mathrm{g}},
\]
where the binomial random variable is independent of $d_{\mathrm{g}}$ (and we recall the definition of $d_{\mathrm{g}}$ from \Cref{sec:further_notation_Gstar}). Also, we have $d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})\ge1$ with probability at least $q$, independently of everything else.

We have
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})}{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})+d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k})+2d}\cdotp_{\mathrm{esc}}\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k}\right]\quad\ge \quad\mathbb{P}\!\left(d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_k)\ge1\right)\cdot\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_k)+2d+1}\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k}\right]\cdotp_{\mathrm{esc}}.
\]

Here
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_k)+2d+1}\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k}\right]\quad\ge\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{Bin}\!\left(k,\frac{\widetilde{C}}{\log\log N}\right)+d_{\mathrm{g}}+2d+2}\right],
\]
where $\mathrm{Bin}\!\left(k,\frac{\widetilde{C}}{\log\log N}\right)$ and $d_{\mathrm{g}}$ are independent. We know that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[d_{\mathrm{g}}\right]\lesssim 1$, hence for a sufficiently large constant $C'$ the event $\{d_{\mathrm{g}}\le C'\}$ has positive probability. Also, for a sufficiently large constant~$C'$ the event $\left\{\mathrm{Bin}\!\left(k,\frac{\widetilde{C}}{\log\log N}\right)\le C'\frac{k}{\log\log N}\right\}$ has positive probability. Together these show that the expectation on the right-hand side is $\gtrsim1\wedge\frac{\log\log N}{k}$, therefore
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})}{d_{\mathrm{r}}(v_{k})+d_{\mathrm{g}}(v_{k})+2d}\cdotp_{\mathrm{esc}}\;\middle\vert\;\mathcal{F}_{k}\right]\quad\gtrsim\quad1\wedge\frac{\log\log N}{k}\:.
\]
This shows that we can choose $(p_k)$ as required.

(C) Concluding the proof:

Now we are ready to upper bound the probability of the event $\left\{|R^Z\capV_{\mathrm{g}}|\ge k,\:\Omega^Z_\mathrm{deg}(k)\right\}$.

If this event holds, then we have $\1{A_0}=....=\1{A_{k-1}}=0$ and up to visiting the $k$th new vertex $v_k$ the walk does not visit any vertex with green degree $>d_{\mathrm{max}}$. This has probability $\le\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\left(1-p_j\right)$. Hence $|R^Y\capV_{\mathrm{g}}|\1{\Omega_\mathrm{deg}}\le_{\mathrm{st}}\mathrm{GGeom}_{\ge1}\left((p_k)\right)$ as required.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{iid_decomp}
Let us consider a random walk $X$ on a random quasi-tree $T$, and let\\ $J:=\max\left\{j\ge0:\:\sigma_j<\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right\}$. Then the following are satisfied.
\begin{itemize}
\item $J\sim\mathrm{GGeom}_{\ge0}\left(\widetilde{p}_0,\widetilde{p},\widetilde{p},...\right)$. \footnote{We recall the notation $\mathrm{GGeom}_{\ge0}\left(\cdot\right)$ from before \Cref{bound_range_in_ball_until_tauatyp}.}
\item Conditional on $J=j\ge1$, the following $j+1$ parts are independent: $\left(T\setminus T(X_{\sigma_1}),(X_t)_{t\le\sigma_1}\right)$, $\left(T\left(X_{\sigma_i}\right)\setminus T\left(X_{\sigma_{i+1}}\right),(X_t)_{t\in\left[\sigma_i,\sigma_{i+1}\right]}\right)$ for $i=1,...,j-1$, and $\left(T\left(X_{\sigma_j}\right),\left(X_t\right)_{t\in\left[\sigma_j,\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right]}\right)$.
\item Conditional on $J=j\ge1$, the following $j-1$ parts are identically distributed, and their distribution does not depend on $j$: $\left(T\left(X_{\sigma_i}\right)\setminus T\left(X_{\sigma_{i+1}}\right),(X_t)_{t\in\left[\sigma_i,\sigma_{i+1}\right]}\right)$ for $i=1,...,j-1$.
\item Conditional on $J\ge1$, the distribution of $\left(T\left(X_{\sigma_J}\right),\left(X_t\right)_{t\in\left[\sigma_J,\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right]}\right)$ does not depend on $J$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{bound_entropy_T}
{Let $T$ be a random quasi-tree as in Definition~\ref{def:random_quasi_tree} and let $\xi$ be a loop-erasure of a simple random walk $X$ on $T$ and $\widetilde{\xi}$ be an independent loop-erasure on $T$.\footnote{{Recall that in the definition of loop-erasures and regenerations we consider the walk only until it first hits an atypical ball.}} Then for any $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$ we have
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{\varphi_1}\in\widetilde{\xi}\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right)\right)^b\1{\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)}\1{\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)}\right]\quad\lesssim\quad1.\]
Furthermore, the same statement holds if we replace $(T,X,\xi,\widetilde{\xi})$ with $(T',X',\xi',\widetilde{\xi}')$, where $(T',X')$ is defined as in \Cref{sec:iid_decomp}, $\xi'$ is the loop-erasure of $X'$, and $\widetilde{\xi}'$ is an independent copy of $\xi'$ conditional on $T'$.}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{speed_concentration}
Let $\nu:=\frac{\mathbb{E}\!\left[\varphi'_1\;\middle\vert\;\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right),\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\right]}{\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sigma'_1\;\middle\vert\;\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right),\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\right]}$, where $\sigma'_1$ and $\varphi'_1$ are the analogues of $\sigma_1$ and $\varphi_1$ for $(T',X')$. Then $\nu\asymp1$, and for any $\theta>0$ there exists $C>0$ such that for all $\ell$ and all sufficiently large $t$ we have
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|d_T(\rho,X_t)-\nu t\right|>C\sqrt{t},\:t\le\sigma_{\ell},\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_{\ell}\right),\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_{\ell}\right)\right)\quad<\quad\theta,
\]
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{s\in[0,t]}d_T(\rho,X_s)>\nu t+2C\sqrt{t}, \:t\le\sigma_{\ell},\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_{\ell}\right),\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_{\ell}\right)\right)\quad<\quad\theta,
\]
where we recall $d_T$ denotes long-range distance in the random quasi-tree $T$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{entropy_concentration}
We use the notation from~\Cref{bound_entropy_T} and let
{\[
\mathfrak{h}:=\quad\frac{1}{\mathbb{E}\!\left[\varphi'_1\1{\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)}\1{\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)}\right]} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi'_{\varphi'_1}\in\widetilde{\xi'}\;\middle\vert\;T',X'\right)\right)\1{\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)}\1{\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)}\right],\qquad\mathfrak{V}:=\log\log N.
\]}

For all $\theta>0$ and $\widehat{C}>0$, there exists a positive constant $C$ so that for all $k\le\widehat{C}\log N=:\ell$ we have


{\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{k}=\widetilde{\xi}_k\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right) -\mathfrak{h} k\right|>C\sqrt{k\mathfrak{V}},\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_{\ell}\right),\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_{\ell}\right)\right)\quad\le\quad\theta.
\]}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{bound_R_sigma1}
There exist constants $C\in(0,\infty)$ and $c\in(0,1)$ with the following property.
If $T$ is a random quasi-tree as in Definition~\ref{def:random_quasi_tree} and $X$ is a random walk on it, then we have
\[|R_{\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}|\quad\le_{\mathrm{st}}\quad C+(\mathrm{Geom}\!\left(c\right))^3,\]
where $R_k$ denotes the range of $X$ up to time $k$, $\tau_{\partial}$ is the first time that the walk has visited $R$ distinct vertices in an $(R+R)$-ball, and we set $\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}=\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}$ in the case that $\sigma_1$ is not defined (i.e.\ there is no regeneration until $\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$).

Furthermore, the same statement holds for $(T',X')$ instead of $(T,X)$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{bound_sigma1}
There exist constants $C\in(0,\infty)$ and $c\in(0,1)$ with the following property. If $T$ is a random quasi-tree as in Definition~\ref{def:random_quasi_tree} and $X$ is a random walk on it, then we have
\[
\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}\quad\le_{\mathrm{st}}\quad C+\left(\mathrm{Geom}\!\left(c\right)\right)^{15},
\]
where $\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}$ is defined as in \Cref{bound_R_sigma1}.

Furthermore, the same statement holds for $(T',X')$ instead of $(T,X)$.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Firstly, we prove that for each level $\ell$ the number of different vertices visited by the walk at level $\ell$ can be bounded as
\begin{align}\label{eq:bound_range_in_one_level}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(|R_{\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}\cap V_\ell|\ge k\right)\quad\lesssim\quad e^{-(\mathrm{const})k}.
\end{align}
Here $V_\ell$ denotes the set of vertices at level $\ell$.

Note that when the walk is at a vertex $v$ that is the $j$th new vertex seen in its $(R+R)$-ball, the probability of crossing a red edge in the next step is $\ge q_j$, where $q_j\asymp1\wedge\frac{\log\log N}{j}$ for $j\le N^{\mathrm{const}}$. (The proof of this is similar to the proof of \Cref{bound_range_in_ball_until_tauatyp} and is omitted.) Also note that $\min_{j\le R}q_j\asymp1$ and by \Cref{transience_until_nonbinary} if the walk crosses a red edge, there is probability at least $p_{\mathrm{esc}}\asymp1$ that it does not backtrack it until $\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$. Together these give \eqref{eq:bound_range_in_one_level}.

Next, we bound the probability of the walk visiting more than $k$ levels until $\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}$ as
\begin{align}\label{eq:bound_sigma1_ge_tauk_prob}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\tau_k<\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}\right)\quad \leq \quad \mathbb{P}\!\left(\tau_k<\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right)\quad\lesssim\quad e^{-(\mathrm{const})\sqrt{k}}.
\end{align}

{If $\tau_k<\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$ then none of the red edges crossed by time $\tau_k$ is a regeneration edge, i.e.\ each of them gets backtracked by time $\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$.}

{In this case at least one of the following events happens: for some $\sqrt{k}\le\ell\le k$ the walk revisits level $\ell-\sqrt{k}$ after hitting level $\ell$, or the walk hits levels $\sqrt{k}$, $\sqrt{k}-1$, $2\sqrt{k}$, $2\sqrt{k}-1$, ... $ k$, $k-1$ in this order.} We can bound the probabilities of these as follows,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{\ell=\sqrt{k}}^{k}\mathbb{P}\!\left(\text{hit level }\ell\text{ and then hit level }\ell-\sqrt{k},\text{ before }\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right)\quad
\lesssim\quad k e^{-(\mathrm{const})\sqrt{k}}\quad\lesssim\quad e^{-(\mathrm{const})\sqrt{k}},
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\text{hit levels }\sqrt{k},\:\sqrt{k}-1,\:2\sqrt{k},\:2\sqrt{k}-1,...\:k,\:k-1\text{ in this order, before }\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right)\:\lesssim\: e^{-(\mathrm{const})\sqrt{k}}.
\end{align*}

Combining these bounds, we get \eqref{eq:bound_sigma1_ge_tauk_prob}.

Using \eqref{eq:bound_range_in_one_level} to bound $\mathbb{P}\!\left(|R_{\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}\cap V_\ell|\ge k^{1/3}\right)$ for each $\ell\le k^{2/3}$ and using \eqref{eq:bound_sigma1_ge_tauk_prob} to bound\\ $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\tau_{k^{2/3}}<\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}\right)$ we get that $\mathbb{P}\!\left(|R_{\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}|\ge k\right)\lesssim e^{-(\mathrm{const})k^{1/3}}$ as required.

This finishes the proof for $(T,X)$.

With an analogous proof, we can show an analogous result for $(T^a,X^a)$, and then we can use that $\tau_{\rho^a}>\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}^a$ has probability bounded away from 0 to get the result for $(T',X')$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Given a random walk $X$ on $T$, let $s_k:=\min\left\{t:\:|R_t|\ge k\right\}$. Then we have
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}\ge2k\right) \quad\le\quad\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}\right|\ge k^{1/5}\right)+\mathbb{P}\!\left(s_{k^{1/5}}\ge 2k,\:\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}>2k\right).
\]
From \Cref{bound_R_sigma1} we know that the first term on the RHS is $\lesssim e^{-(\mathrm{const})k^{1/15}}$.

Now we bound the second term. Let $R_{k^{1/5}}=\{v_1,...,v_{k^{1/5}}\}$ where $v_i$ are in the order $X$ first visits them. Then
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(s_{k^{1/5}}\ge 2k,\:\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}>2k\right)\quad& \le\quad\sum_{j=0}^{k^{1/5}-1}\mathbb{P}\!\left(s_{j+1}-s_{j}\ge2k^{4/5}\right)\quad\\
&\le\quad\sum_{j=0}^{k^{1/5}-1}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{P}_{v_j}\!\left(\tau_{\{v_1,...,v_{j}\}^c}>2k^{4/5}\;\middle\vert\;T,v_1,...,v_j\right)\right]
\end{align*}

Given $T$ and $v_1,...,v_{j}$ we can bound $\mathbb{P}_{v_j}\!\left(\tau_{\{v_1,...,v_{j}\}^c}>2k^{4/5}\;\middle\vert\;T,v_1,...,v_j\right)$ as follows. Let $H$ be a graph with vertex set $\{v_1,...,v_j,v_{j,\partial}\}$ obtained by contracting $\{v_1,...,v_{j}\}^c$ into a single vertex $v_{j,\partial}$ and for each $i$ in case there are multiple edges between $v_i$ and $v_{j,\partial}$, deleting all of them except for one. By the commute time identity~\cite[Corollary 2.21]{prob-on-trees-and-networks} we know that for any $u\in\{v_1,...,v_j\}$ a SRW on $H$ from $u$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}_{u}\!\left[\tau_{v_{j,\partial}}\right]\le e(H)R_{\mathrm{eff}}^{H}\left(u,\:v_{j,\partial}\right)$ where $e(H)\le j^2$ is the number of edges in $H$ and $R_{\mathrm{eff}}^{H}\left(u,\:v_{j,\partial}\right)\le j$ is the effective resistance between $u$ and $v_{j,\partial}$. Then $\mathbb{P}_{u}\!\left(\tau_{v_{j,\partial}}>2j^3\right)\le\frac12$ for any $u$, hence
\[
\mathbb{P}_{v_j}\!\left(\tau_{\{v_1,...,v_{j}\}^c}>2k^{4/5}\;\middle\vert\;T,v_1,...,v_j\right)\quad\le\quad\mathbb{P}_{v_{j}}\!\left(\tau_{v_{j,\partial}}>2k^{4/5}\right)\quad\le\quad2^{-k^{1/5}}.
\]

Taking a union bound over $j$ we get that $\mathbb{P}\!\left(s_{k^{1/5}}\ge 2k,\:\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}>2k\right)\lesssim k^{1/5}e^{-(\mathrm{const})k^{1/5}}\lesssim e^{-(\mathrm{const})k^{1/5}}$. This finishes the proof for $(T,X)$.

With an analogous proof we can also show that for $(T^a,X^a)$ we have $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sigma^a_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}^a\wedge\tau_{\partial}^a\ge k\right)\lesssim e^{-(\mathrm{const})k^{1/15}}$. Then using that $\tau_{\rho^a}>\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}^a$ has probability bounded away from 0, we also get the result for $(T',X')$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:Hb}
For $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$ and for a sequence $(p_i)$ of real numbers taking values in $[0,1]$ let
\[H_{b}\left(p_1,p_2,...\right):=\quad\sum_{i}p_i(-\log p_i)^b,\]
and for a random variable $W$ taking values in a countable set $\mathcal{W}$ let
\[H_{b}\left(W\right):=\quad\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}}\mathbb{P}\!\left(W=w\right)\left(-\log\mathbb{P}\!\left(W=w\right)\right)^b.\]
In both cases, $p(-\log p)^b$ is considered to be $0$ when $p=0$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
\label{def:Hb_conditional}
For $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$ and for random variables $W$ and $Z$ taking values in countable sets $\mathcal{W}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ respectively let
\begin{align*}H_{b}\left(W\midZ\right):&=\quad\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}}\mathbb{P}\!\left(Z=z\right)H_{b}\left(W|Z=z\right)\\
&=\quad\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}}\mathbb{P}\!\left(Z=z\right)\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}}\mathbb{P}\left(W=w\;\middle\vert\;Z=z\right){}\left(-\log\mathbb{P}\left(W=w\;\middle\vert\;Z=z\right){}\right)^b.
\end{align*}
Here $\mathbb{P}\!\left(Z=z\right)\mathbb{P}\left(W=w\;\middle\vert\;Z=z\right){}\left(-\log\mathbb{P}\left(W=w\;\middle\vert\;Z=z\right){}\right)^b$ is considered to be $0$ when\\ $\mathbb{P}\!\left(Z=z\right)=0$ or $\mathbb{P}\left(W=w\;\middle\vert\;Z=z\right){}=0$.

We can also extend the definition to the case when $Z$ takes values in an uncountable set $\mathcal{Z}$, but for almost all $z\in\mathcal{Z}$, the random variable $\left(W\mid Z=z\right)$ takes values from a countable set, by considering $H_{b}\left(W|Z=z\right)$ and taking an expectation over $Z$.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{def:HbA_and_HbA_conditional}
For $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$, random variables $W$ and $Z$ taking values in countable sets $\mathcal{W}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ respectively, and event $A$, let
\begin{align*}
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\right):&=\quad\sum_{w\in\mathcal{W}}\mathbb{P}\!\left(W=w,\:A\right)\left(-\log\mathbb{P}\!\left(W=w,\:A\right)\right)^b\\
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\midZ\right):&=\quad\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}}\mathbb{P}\!\left(Z=z\right)H_{b}^{A}\left(W|Z=z\right).
\end{align*}
We interpret the cases when one of the probabilities is 0 as before. We extend the definition to the case when $\mathcal{Z}$ is uncountable but $\left(W\mid Z=z\right)$ takes values from a countable set for almost all $z\in\mathcal{Z}$ analogously to \Cref{def:Hb_conditional}.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
First note that
{\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{\varphi_1}\in\widetilde{\xi}\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right)\right)^b\1{\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)}\1{\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)}\right]\quad\le\quad H_{b}^{A}\left(\xi_{\varphi_1}\midT\right),\]}
where $A=\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)$.

By \Cref{HbA_cond_properties}\eqref{item:HbA_cond_i} we have
\[
H_{b}^{A}\left(\xi_{\varphi_1}\midT\right)\quad\lesssim\quad H_{b}^{A}\left(X_{\sigma_1}\midT,\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)+H_{b}^{A}\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\midT\right).
\]

From \Cref{HbA_cond_properties}\eqref{item:HbA_cond_i} and \Cref{bound_R_sigma1} we get that
\[
H_{b}^{A}\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\midT\right)\:\le\: H_{b}^{A}\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)+O(1) \:=\:H_{b}^{A}\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}\right|\right)+O(1)\:\lesssim\: H_{b}\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1\wedge\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\wedge\tau_{\partial}}\right|\right)+O(1)\:\lesssim\:1.
\]

Also by \Cref{HbA_cond_properties}\eqref{item:HbA_cond_iii}, we have
\[
H_{b}^{A}\left(X_{\sigma_1}\midT,\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)\quad\lesssim\quad \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\log V_T\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)\right)^b\1{A}\right]+\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(A\;\middle\vert\;T,\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)\left(-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(A\;\middle\vert\;T,\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)\right)^b\right]
\]
where $V_T(r)$ denotes the volume of the ball of radius $r$ around the root in $T$.

The second expectation is $\lesssim1$ since the function $p(-\log p)^b$ is bounded for $p\in[0,1]$. We can bound the first expectation as follows.

Let $\lambda\in\left(0,\frac{1}{\log(2d+3)}\right)$ be a constant. Then
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\log V_T\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)\right)^b\1{A}\right]\quad\le\quad\sum_{s\ge1}\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left(\log V_T\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\right)\right)^b\1{A}\ge s\right)+1
\]
\[
\le\quad\sum_{s\ge1}\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\ge\lambda s^{1/b},A\right)+ \sum_{s\ge1}\mathbb{P}\!\left(V_T\left(\lambda s^{1/b}\right)\ge \exp\left(s^{1/b}\right),A\right)+1.
\]

From \Cref{bound_R_sigma1} we get
\[
\sum_{s\ge1}\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|\ge\lambda s^{1/b},A\right)\quad=\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\frac{\left|R_{\sigma_1}\right|}{\lambda}\right)^b\1A\right]\quad\lesssim\quad1.
\]

Also, using \Cref{T_volume_tail_bound} and that $\lambda<\frac{1}{\log(2d+3)}$ we get that
\[
\sum_{s\ge1}\mathbb{P}\!\left(V_T\left(\lambda s^{1/b}\right)\ge\exp\left(s^{1/b}\right),A\right)\quad\le\quad \sum_{s\ge1}\exp\left(\frac14-\frac14\exp\left(s^{1/b}\right)(2d+3)^{-\lambda s^{1/b}}\right)
\]
\[
\asymp\quad\sum_{s\ge1}\exp\left(-\frac14\exp\left(s^{1/b}\left(1-\lambda\log(2d+3)\right)\right)\right)\quad\lesssim\quad1.
\]
This finishes the proof for $(T,X,\widetilde{\xi})$. The proof for $(T',X',\widetilde{\xi}')$ is analogous.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Using \Cref{bound_sigma1} and that the events $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)$ and $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)$ have probability bounded away from 0, we get that the variables $\left(\sigma'_1\mid\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\right)$, $\left(\varphi'_1\mid\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\right)$, $\left(\sigma_1\mid\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)\right)$ and $\left(\varphi_1\mid\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)\right)$ each have expectation $\asymp1$ and variance $\lesssim1$.

This shows $\nu\asymp1$.

From \Cref{iid_decomp} we know that conditional on $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)$, the variables
\[
\left((\sigma_k-\sigma_{k-1}),(\varphi_k-\varphi_{k-1})\right)_{k=2,...,\ell}
\]
are independent and have the same distribution as $\left(\left(\sigma'_1,\varphi'_1\right)|\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\right)$. They are also independent of the pair $(\sigma_1,\varphi_1)$, which is distributed as $\left((\sigma_1,\varphi_1)|\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_1\right)\right)$. Using this and the bounds on the expectation and variance of these variables, we get that for any $\theta$, for sufficiently large $C$ and for each $i\le\ell$ we have
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|d_T(\rho,X_{\sigma_i})-\nu\sigma_i\right|>C\sqrt{\sigma_i},\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_\ell\right),\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)\right)\hspace{5cm}\\
\le\quad\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\left|d_T(\rho,X_{\sigma_i})-\nu\sigma_i\right|>C\sqrt{\sigma_i}\;\middle\vert\;\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_\ell\right),\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)\right)\quad<\quad\theta.
\end{align*}

We can extend the result for all times $t$, and we can prove the second bound similarly to the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.19]{weighted_random_matching}. For the parts of the proof where we want to use the concentration of the sum of iid random variables we condition on $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)$, while for parts where we want to bound the probability of backtracking many levels, we just include the event $\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_\ell\right)$ in the probability.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Let us write $A_{i}:=\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma_{i-1},\sigma_i\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma_{i-1},\sigma_i\right)$, $A_{\le j}:=\bigcap_{i\le j}A_i$, $A_{\ge j}:=\bigcap_{j\le i\le\ell}A_i$ and $A:=A_{\le\ell}$. Let $\Delta_i=\varphi_i-\varphi_{i-1}$.

{Also let $Y_i:=-\log\frac{\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{\varphi_i}\in\widetilde{\xi}\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right) }{\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{\varphi_{i-1}}\in\widetilde{\xi}\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right)}$ for $i\geq 2$ and let $Y_1:= -\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{\varphi_1}\in\widetilde{\xi}\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right)$.}
 Then 
{\[
 -\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi_{\varphi_k}\in\widetilde{\xi}\;\middle\vert\;T,X\right)\quad =\quad \sum_{i=1}^{k}Y_i.
 \]}


By Markov's inequality
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|\sum_{i=1}^{k}Y_i-\varphi_k\mathfrak{h}\right|>C\sqrt{k\mathfrak{V}},A\right)\quad\le\quad\frac{\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^{k}(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h})\right)^2\1{A}\right]}{C^2k\mathfrak{V}}.
\]
In what follows, we will prove that
\begin{align}\label{eq:bound_sum_Yisq}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^{k}(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h})\right)^2\1{A}\right]\quad\lesssim\quad k\log\log N,
\end{align}
which implies the desired concentration bound along the regeneration times. Once we have this, we can extend the result for all times similarly to the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.20]{weighted_random_matching}. The details of this are omitted.

In what follows, we work towards the proof of \eqref{eq:bound_sum_Yisq} by establishing bounds for
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)^2\1{A}\right]\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\right]
\]
for each $i$ and each $i\ne j$

Note that $(Y_i)_{i\ge2}$ is stationary and each term is distributed as {$Y':=-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\xi'_{\varphi'_1}\in\widetilde{\xi}'\;\middle\vert\;T',X'\right)$. }
Let us define $A'_1:=\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\sigma'_1\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(\sigma'_1\right)$ corresponding to the walk $X'$ in the definition of $Y'$.

Also note that $Y_i=-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(X_{\sigma_i}\in\xi(i)\;\middle\vert\;(X_t)_{t\ge\sigma_{i-1}},T(X_{\sigma_{i-1}})\right)$,
where $\xi(i)$ is the loop-erasure of a random walk $X^i$ on $T(X_{\sigma_{i-1}})$ started from $X_{\sigma_{i-1}}$, {stopped upon hitting an atypical ball}\footnote{{Here we are using that for a given realisation of a quasi-tree $T^a$ (with parent of the root $\rho^a$) the distribution of the loop-erasure of the simple random walk (stopped at $\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$) from $\rho$ is the same as the distribution of the loop-erasure of the simple random walk (stopped at $\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$) from $\rho$ conditioned on not hitting $\rho^a$.}}, but otherwise independent of $(X_t)_{t\ge\sigma_{i-1}}$.

Firstly, we prove that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\right]\lesssim1$ for all $i,j\in\{1,2,...,k\}$.
\begin{itemize}
\item From \Cref{bound_entropy_T} we know that
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_1^2\1{A}\right]\quad\le\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_1^2\1{A_1}\right]\quad\lesssim\quad1,\]
and that for any $i\ge2$ we have
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_i^2\1{A}\right]\quad\le\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_i^2\1{A_i}\right]\quad=\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[(Y')^2\1{A'_1}\right]\quad\lesssim\quad1.\]
Also, by \Cref{bound_entropy_T} we have $\mathfrak{h}\lesssim1$ and by \Cref{bound_sigma1} we have $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Delta_i^2\1{A}\right]\lesssim1$, hence for each $i\in\{1,2,...,\ell\}$ we have
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)^2\1{A}\right]\quad\lesssim\quad1.\]
\item Using Cauchy-Schwarz we get that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\right]\lesssim1$ for any $i,j\in\{1,2,...,k\}$.
\end{itemize}
Now we proceed to show that there exist positive constants $u$ and $U$ such that for all $2\le i<j\le\ell$ with $j-i\ge U\log\log N$ we have
\begin{align}\label{eq:bound_YiYj}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\right]\quad\lesssim\quad e^{-u\left(\frac{j-i}{\log\log N}\right)^{1/3}}+\frac{1}{\log N}\:.
\end{align}
Since $k\le\ell\asymp\log N$, this concludes the proof of \eqref{eq:bound_sum_Yisq}.
\begin{itemize}
\item We define
\begin{align*}
B_{i,j}:=&\quad\left\{\left|R_{[\sigma_{i-1},\sigma_{i}]}\right|\le \frac{j-i}{U'\log\log N}\right\},\\
Y_{i,j}:=&\quad-\log\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(X_{\sigma_i}\in\xi(i,j)\;\middle\vert\;X,T(X_{\sigma_{i-1}})\right),
\end{align*}
where $U'$ is a sufficiently large constant, $R_{[t_1,t_2]}$ denotes the range of $X$ in the time interval $[t_1,t_2]$, and $\xi(i,j)$ is the loop-erasure of $X^i$ up to the first time that it hits level $\varphi_{j-1}$ {or hits an atypical ball, whichever occurs first}. (Recall that $X^i$ is a random walk on $T(X_{\sigma_{i-1}})$ started from $X_{\sigma_{i-1}}$, but otherwise independent from $(X_t)_{t\ge\sigma_{i-1}}$.)
\item Then
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \label{item:indep} $B_{i,j}$ and $Y_{i,j}\1{B_{i,j}}$ are independent of $Y_j\1{A_{\ge j}}$,\\
${}$\hfill(since they depend on different layers between regenerations)
\item \label{item:bound_prob} $\mathbb{P}\!\left(B_{i,j}^c\cap A_i\right)\lesssim e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot\left(\frac{j-i}{\log\log N}\right)^{1/3}}$,\hfill(from \Cref{bound_R_sigma1})
\item \label{item:bound_diff} $|Y_i-Y_{i,j}|\1{B_{i,j}}\1{A_i}\le e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot(j-i)}$.\hfill (see proof below)
\item \label{item:bound_Y} $Y_{i,j}\1{B_{i,j}}\1{A_i}\lesssim(j-i)$.\hfill (see proof below)
\end{enumerate}
\item We can prove~\eqref{item:bound_diff} as follows. Let
\[Z_i:=\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(X_{\sigma_i}\in\xi(i)\;\middle\vert\;X,T(X_{\sigma_{i-1}})\right)\quad\text{and}\quad Z_{i,j}:=\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(X_{\sigma_i}\in\xi(i,j)\;\middle\vert\;X,T(X_{\sigma_{i-1}})\right).\]
Then $|Y_i-Y_{i,j}|\le\frac{|Z_i-Z_{i,j}|}{Z_i\wedge Z_{i,j}}$. Note that having $X_{\sigma_i}\in\xi(i)$, but $X_{\sigma_i}\not\in\xi(i,j)$ or the other way around would require backtracking $\ge(j-i)$ levels. The probability of backtracking $\ge(j-i)$ levels without visiting an atypical ball is $\le e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot(j-i)}$. Also, by considering a path from $X_{\sigma_{i-1}}$ to $X_{\sigma_i}$ on $R_{[\sigma_{i-1},\sigma_{i}]}$
and noting that on event $A_i$ each vertex on the path has degree $\lesssim\log N$ we get that on event $B_{i,j}\cap A_i$ we have $(Z_{i}\wedge Z_{i,j})\gtrsim e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot\log\log N\cdot\frac{j-i}{U'\log\log N}}$. Choosing $U'$ to be sufficiently large this shows that $|Y_i-Y_{i,j}|\1{B_{i,j}}\1{A_i}\le e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot(j-i)}$.
\item Part~\eqref{item:bound_Y} also follows from noting that on the event $B_{i,j}\cap A_i$ we have $Z_{i,j}\gtrsim e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot\log\log N\cdot\frac{j-i}{U'\log\log N}}$.
\item Using Cauchy-Schwarz, we get that 
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\1{B_{i,j}^c}\right]\:\le\:\left(\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)^4\1{A}\right]\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)^4\1{A}\right]\mathbb{P}\!\left(B_{i,j}^c\cap A\right)^2\right)^{\frac14}.
\]
From \Cref{bound_entropy_T}, \Cref{bound_sigma1} and~\eqref{item:bound_prob} we get that this is $\lesssim e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot\left(\frac{j-i}{\log\log N}\right)^{1/3}}$.
\item Also, we have
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\1{B_{i,j}}\right]\\
&=\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-Y_{i,j}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\1{B_{i,j}}\right]+ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_{i,j}-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A}\1{B_{i,j}}\right]\\
&\le\quad\left(\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_i-Y_{i,j}\right)^2\1{A_i}\1{B_{i,j}}\right]\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)^2\1{A_j}\right]\right)^{\frac12}\\
&\hspace{3cm}+\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_{i,j}-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A_{\le j-1}}\1{B_{i,j}}\right] \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A_{\ge j}}\right].
\end{align*}
From \Cref{bound_entropy_T} and~\eqref{item:bound_diff} we get that the first term in the last line is $\lesssim e^{-\mathrm{const}\cdot(j-i)}$.
\item We can write
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A_{\ge j}}\right]\quad=\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A_{j}}\right]-\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A_j}\1{A_{\ge j+1}^c}\right].
\]
Note that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_j\1{A_j}\right]=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Delta_j\1{A_j}\right]\mathfrak{h}$, hence the first term is 0. Also, by Cauchy-Schwarz, the second term has absolute value
\[\le\quad\left(\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_j-\Delta_j\mathfrak{h}\right)^2\1{A_j}\right]\mathbb{P}\!\left(A_{\ge j+1}^c\right)\right)^{\frac12}.\]
We can show that this is $\lesssim\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^2$ by using \Cref{bound_entropy_T} and that by \Cref{rmk:atypical_ball}, \Cref{bound_atyp_prob} and \Cref{bound_sigma1} we have $\mathbb{P}\!\left(A_{\ge j+1}^c\right)\lesssim(\ell-j)\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^5\lesssim\left(\frac{1}{\log N}\right)^{4}$.
\item Using~\eqref{item:bound_Y} and that $\mathfrak{h}\lesssim1$ and $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Delta_i\1{A_i}\right]\lesssim1$, we also get
\[\left|\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(Y_{i,j}-\Delta_i\mathfrak{h}\right)\1{A_{\le j-1}}\1{B_{i,j}}\right]\right|\quad\lesssim\quad j-i\quad\lesssim\quad\log N.\]
\item Putting these bounds together, we conclude the proof of \eqref{eq:bound_YiYj}.\qedhere
\end{itemize}
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{def:W_Wtil}
For a long-range edge $e$ in a quasi-tree $T$ let
\[
W_T(e):=\quad -\log\mathbb{P}_{\rho}\!\left(e\in\xi\;\middle\vert\;T\right),\qquad
\widetilde{W}_T(e):=\quad -\log\mathbb{P}_{\rho}\!\left(X_{\tau_\ell(e)}=e^+\;\middle\vert\;T\right).\qedhere
\]
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{compare_W_Wtil}
There exists a positive constant $C$ so that for any realisation $T$ of a random quasi-tree and any long-range edge $e$ in $T$ we have
\[
W_T(e)\quad\ge\quad\widetilde{W}_T(e)-CR^4.
\]
Also,
\[
W_T(e)\quad\le\quad\widetilde{W}_T(e)+\log\left(\frac1p_{\mathrm{esc}}\right),
\]
where $p_{\mathrm{esc}}$ is the constant from \Cref{transience_until_nonbinary}.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
We drop the conditioning on $T$ from the notation.

The proof of the first bound follows the proof of~\cite[Lemma 4.3]{random_matching} with the following modifications.

Instead of $\infty$ we write $\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}$.

Note that in a typical $(R+R)$-ball each vertex has degree $\led_{\mathrm{max}}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$, hence for any two vertices of the ball there is a path from one to the other which has probability at least $\left(\frac{1}{d_{\mathrm{max}}}\right)^{4R}\ge\exp\left(-cR^2\right)$. Hence~\cite[(4.6)]{random_matching} holds for $i\le\ell(e)-c_3R^2$, and the right-hand side of~\cite[(4.7)]{random_matching} becomes $\exp\left(-cR^2\right)$.

The second bound is immediate, since \[\mathbb{P}_{\rho}\!\left(e\in\xi\right)\quad\ge\quad\mathbb{P}_{\rho}\!\left(X_{\tau_{\ell(e)}}=e^+\right)\mathbb{P}_{e^+}\!\left(\tau_{e^-}>\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right)\quad\ge\quad\mathbb{P}_{\rho}\!\left(X_{\tau_{\ell(e)}}=e^+\right)p_{\mathrm{esc}},\]
using Corollary~\ref{transience_until_nonbinary} for the last inequality.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{def:trunc}
Let us consider any realisation $T$ of a random quasi-tree. For a positive constant $A$ and a long-range edge $e$ in $T$, we define the corresponding \emph{truncation event} as
\[
\mathrm{Tr}\left(e,A\right):=\quad\left\{\widetilde{W}_T(e)>\frac12(1+c^+_L)\log N+A\sqrt{\frac{\mathfrak{V}\log N}{\mathfrak{h}}}\right\},
\]
where $\mathfrak{h}$ and $\mathfrak{V}$ are as in \Cref{entropy_concentration}.
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{bound_trunc_prob}
For any $\theta\in(0,1)$ there exists $A$ such that for any realisation of $T$
\[
\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\bigcup_{t\le\tau_{L^+}}\mathrm{Tr}\left(\left(X_{t-1},X_t\right),A\right),\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\tau_{L^+}\right),\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\tau_{L^+}\right)\;\middle\vert\;T\right)\quad<\quad\theta.
\]
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The proof is analogous to the proof of~\cite[Lemma 4.5]{random_matching}. We need that
\[
\sqrt{\frac{\mathfrak{V}\log N}{\mathfrak{h}}}\quad\gtrsim\quad R^4+\sqrt{L^+\mathfrak{V}},
\]
which indeed holds since $L^+\asymp\frac{\log N}{\mathfrak{h}}\asymp\log N$ and $R\asymp\log\log N$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{def:truncprime}
Let us consider any realisation $T$ of a random quasi-tree. For a long-range edge $e$ in $T$, we define the corresponding \emph{level $\left(L^--K\right)$ truncation event} as
\[
\mathrm{Tr}'\left(e\right):=\quad\left\{\widetilde{W}_T(e)<\frac12\log N+\sqrt{\log N}\right\} \cap\left\{\ell(e)=L^--K\right\}.\qedhere
\]
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{bound_truncprime_prob}
For any $\theta\in(0,1)$ for sufficiently large values of $C_L^-$ we have
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\mathrm{Tr}'\left(\left(X_{\tau_{(L^--K)}-1},X_{\tau_{(L^--K)}}\right)\right),\:\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\tau_{(L^--K)}\right),\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\tau_{(L^--K)}\right)\right)\quad<\quad\theta.
\]
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
We use \Cref{compare_W_Wtil} and \Cref{entropy_concentration}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{def:Kroot}
We say that a vertex $x$ in $G^*$ is a \emph{$K$-root} if in the quasi-tree $T_x(G^*)$ corresponding to $G^*$ (see \Cref{def:quasi-tree_of_Gstar}) the vertices in the first $K$ levels correspond to different vertices of $G^*$.
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
\label{def:That}
Given a quasi-tree $T$, a corresponding \emph{quasi-tree with blue half-edges}, denoted by $\widehat{T}$, is obtained by adding $d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}d_{\mathrm{b}}$ blue half-edges to each vertex $v$ of $T$, independently of each other and everything else.

{Given the graph $G^*$ and a vertex $x$, the corresponding quasi-tree with blue half-edges $\widehat{T}_x(G^*)$ is obtained from $T_x(G^*)$ by adding $d_{\mathrm{b}}(\iota(v))$ blue half-edges to each of its vertices $v$.}
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
\label{def:nice}
We say that a vertex $x$ in $G^*$ is \emph{nice} if it satisfies both of the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $x$ is a $K$-root.
\item $\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\tau_K\right),\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\tau_K\right),\:\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}>\tau_K\;\middle\vert\;{\widehat{T}_{x}(G^*)}\right)\gec_{\mathrm{nice}}$, where $\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}$ denotes the first time that the walk crosses a blue (half-)edge, and  $c_{\mathrm{nice}}\in(0,1)$ is a sufficiently small constant to be specified later.
\end{enumerate}

We denote the set of nice vertices by $V_{\mathrm{nice}}$.
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
\label{def:almost_nice}
We say that a vertex $x$ in $G^*$ is \emph{almost nice}, if there exists a red or a blue edge $e$ emanating from $x$ such that the vertex $x$ satisfies the conditions of \Cref{def:nice} in the graph~$G^*\setminus\{e\}$, and the other endpoint of $e$ is not contained in the neighbourhood of $x$ up to $K$ levels in~$G^*\setminus\{e\}$. We will call such an edge $e$ a \emph{distinguished edge} corresponding to $x$.

We denote the set of almost nice vertices by $V'_{\mathrm{nice}}$.
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{niceprime_hit_level_K}
{Let $x\inV'_{\mathrm{nice}}$ and let $e=\{x,x^a\}$ be a corresponding distinguished edge. Let $\widehat{T}_{x}^a(G^*)$ be obtained by considering the quasi-tree with blue half-edges $\widehat{T}_{x}(G^*\setminus\{e\})$ corresponding to $G^*\setminus\{e\}$ around $x$, and adding an additional edge $\{x,x^a\}$ to a new vertex $x^a$. Then a simple random walk on $\widehat{T}_{x}^a(G^*)$ satisfies
\[\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(\tau_K\right),\:\Omega_{\partial}\left(\tau_K\right),\:\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}>\tau_K,\:\tau_{x^a}>\tau_K\;\middle\vert\;\widehat{T}_{x}^a(G^*)\right)\quad\ge\quadc_{\mathrm{nice}}',\]
where $c_{\mathrm{nice}}'$ is a positive constant depending on $c_{\mathrm{nice}}$.}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Let us drop the subscript $x$ and argument $G^*$ of the trees and drop the conditioning on the trees from the notation. Let us also write $\Omega(s)=\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(s\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(s\right)\cap\{\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}>s\}\cap\{\tau_{x^a}>s\}$ when considering a walk on $\widehat{T}^a$, and $\Omega(s)=\Omega_{\mathrm{typ}}\left(s\right)\cap\Omega_{\partial}\left(s\right)\cap\{\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}>s\}$ when considering a walk on $\widehat{T}$.

By considering the number of times that the walk returns to $x$, we see that
\begin{align}
\nonumber
&\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}^a}\!\left(\Omega(\tau_K)\right)\quad=\quad\sum_{k\ge0}\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}^a}\!\left(\Omega(\tau_K),\text{ exactly }k\text{ returns to }x\right)\\
\nonumber
&=\quad\sum_{k\ge0}\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}^a}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_x^+)\right)^k \mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}^a}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_K)\right)\quad=\quad \frac{\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}^a}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_K)\right)}{1-\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}^a}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_x^+)\right)}\\
\label{eq:That_vs_T_prob}
&=\quad\frac{\frac{\deg(x)}{\deg(x)+1}\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_K)\right)}{1-\frac{\deg(x)}{\deg(x)+1}\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_x^+)\right)}\quad=\quad \frac{\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_K)\right)}{\frac{1}{\deg(x)}+1-\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_x^+)\right)}\:,
\end{align}
where $\deg(x)$ denotes the degree of $x$ in $\widehat{T}$.

Note that
\begin{align*}
1-\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_x^+)\right)\quad\ge\quad1-\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right)\quad=\quad\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_{\mathrm{atyp}}\right)\quad\gtrsim\quad\frac{1}{\deg(x)},
\end{align*}
where in the $\gtrsim$ we used \Cref{transience_until_nonbinary}. Then
\begin{align*}
\eqref{eq:That_vs_T_prob}\quad\asymp\quad\frac{\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+>\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_K)\right)}{1-\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\tau_x^+<\tau_K,\:\Omega(\tau_x^+)\right)}\quad=\quad\mathbb{P}_{x}^{\widehat{T}}\!\left(\Omega(\tau_K)\right),
\end{align*}
which finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{transition_probs_on_Vnice}
There exist positive constants $c$ and $C$ such that with high probability $G^*$ has the following property. Let $X$ be a simple random walk on $G^*$ and let $\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}^{(2)}$ be the second time that it crosses a blue edge. Then for all $x\inV'_{\mathrm{nice}}$ and $y\inV_{\mathrm{nice}}$ such that the neighbourhoods of $x$ and $y$ up to the first $K$ levels are disjoint and do not contain the other endpoint of the distinguished edge $e_x$ associated to $x$, we have
\[\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(X_{\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}^{(2)}-1}=y,\:\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}^{(2)}\le C\log N\;\middle\vert\;G^*\right)\quad\ge\quad c\frac{\log N}{N}d_{\mathrm{b}}(y)\:.\]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{Succhat_prob}
There exists $\theta\in(0,1)$ such that we have
\[
\mathbb{P}_{}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{x,y}\!\left(\widehat{\Omega}_{\mathrm{succ}}\;\middle\vert\;\widehat{\mathcal{F}}_{L_x+L_y}\right)>\theta\;\middle\vert\;\left\{\widehat{T}^a_{x,K},\widehat{T}_{y,K}\right\}\right)\quad\ge\quad1-o\left(\frac{1}{N^2}\right).
\]
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{bound_prob_specific_blue_edge}
For each blue half-edge $e$ in $\widehat{T}_x$ we have
\[
\mathbb{P}_{x}\!\left(\widehat{Z}^{(1)}_{\tau_{\mathrm{blue}}}=e,\:\widehat{Z}^{(1)}\text{ satisfies the conditions of }\widehat{\Omega}_{\mathrm{succ}}\;\middle\vert\;\widehat{\mathcal{F}}_{L_x+L_y}\right)\quad\le\quad\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\log N}}.
\]
We also have an analogous bound for $\widehat{Z}^{(2)}$ and $\widehat{T}_y$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let $f$ be the level $L^--M$ ancestor of $e$.
