Note that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{v\in S}\deg(v)\right]\asymp\mathrm{Var}\left(\sum_{v\in S}\deg(v)\right)\asymp n^d$, so whp $\sum_{v\in S}\deg(v)\asymp n^d$. Similarly, whp $\sum_{v\in S^c}\deg(v)\asymp n^d$.

Also, we have
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{rgb}} y}\right]\quad=\quad\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}p_{x,y}\quad\asymp\quad\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}\frac{1}{|x-y|^d},\]
\[\mathrm{Var}\left(\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{rgb}} y}\right)\quad=\quad\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}p_{x,y}(1-p_{x,y})\quad\asymp\quad\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}p_{x,y}.\]

For a given distance $r$, we get that there are $\asymp n^{d-1}r^d$ pairs $x\in S$, $y\in S^c$ with $|x-y|=r$. Hence $\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}p_{x,y}\asymp\frac{n^d}{\log n}$. This shows that whp $\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}\1{x\sim y}=\sum_{x\in S,\:y\in S^c}\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{rgb}} y}+n^{d-1}\asymp\frac{n^d}{\log n}$.

So overall we get that whp $\Phi^*\le\frac{Q(S,S^c)}{\pi(S)\wedge\pi(S^c)}\asymp\frac{1}{\log n}\asymp\frac{1}{\log N}$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{far_from_bipartite_asymp} For any constant $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a constant $C>0$ with the following property. If a graph $H=(V,E)$ is such that for any partition $A\sqcup B $ of $V$ we have $|E(A)|+|E(B)|\ge\varepsilon|E|$, then a simple random walk on $H$ satisfies $t_\mathrm{rel}\let_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\le Ct_\mathrm{rel}$.

(For a set $S\subseteq V$ of vertices, $E(S)$ denotes the set of edges in $E$ with both endpoints in $S$.)
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{Gstar_far_from_bipartite}
There exists a positive constant $c$ such that whp $G^*$ has the following property. For any partition of $V=A\sqcup B$ of its vertices, we have $|E(A)|+|E(B)|\ge c|E|$.
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
In what follows, we assume for convenience that $n$ is even, but a very similar proof works for odd $n$. From \Cref{total_degree} we know that whp $|E|\le(2d+2)N$, so it is sufficient to show that whp for any partition $V=A\sqcup B$ we have $|E(A)|+|E(B)|\gtrsim N$.

Let us say that a vertex $v\in\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is even if the sum of its coordinates is even, and it is odd otherwise. Let us partition $V$ into pairs of adjacent vertices, of the form $\left((2k,i_2,...,i_d),(2k+1,i_2,...,i_d)\right)$ and let us identify the pairs with $W:=\mathbb{Z}_{n/2}\times\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{d-1}$ the natural way.

Consider a partition $A\sqcup B$ of $V$.

Let $S\subseteq W$ correspond to the pairs where both vertices are in $A$ or both are in $B$, and let $U\subseteq W$ correspond to the pairs where the even vertex (i.e.\ the vertex from the pair where the sum of the coordinates is even) is in $A$. This defines a bijection between partitions $A\sqcup B$ of $V$ and pairs $(S,U)$ of subsets of $W$.

Note that for any $s\in S$, the black edge between the two vertices of the corresponding pair runs within $A$ or within $B$. Also note that for any $u\in U$, $v\in U^c$ with $u\sim v$ in $\mathbb{Z}_{n/2}\times\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{d-1}$, there is a black edge between two of the four vertices corresponding to the pairs $u$ and $v$ that runs within $A$ or within $B$. Hence for any positive constant $\varepsilon$: if $|S|\ge \varepsilon N$ or $\sum_{u\in U,\:v\in U^c}\1{u\sim v}\ge \varepsilon N$, then we have $|E(A)|+|E(B)|\ge \varepsilon N$.

In what follows, for any partition satisfying $|S|\le \varepsilon N$ with a sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, we bound the probability of $|E(A)|+|E(B)|\le c N$ (where $c$ is an absolute constant). Then we bound the number of partitions with $|S|\le \varepsilon N$ and $\sum_{u\in U,\:v\in U^c}\1{u\sim v}\le\varepsilon N$. We conclude the proof by taking a union bound over these partitions.

Let us consider a partition $V=A\sqcup B$ with $|S|\le \varepsilon N$.

Let $S'$ be a set that contains exactly one vertex from each of the pairs in $S$, and let $A'$ be a set that contains the vertices in $A$ except for the ones in the pairs in $S$.

A quick calculation shows that $\sum\limits_{x,y\in A'\cup S'}p_{x,y}\asymp N$. Also, $\sum\limits_{x\in S',y\in A'\cup S'}p_{x,y}\le|S'|\le \varepsilon N$, hence for sufficiently small values of $\varepsilon$ we have $\sum\limits_{x,y\in A'}p_{x,y}\ge 2cN$ where $c$ is an absolute constant.

Then using \Cref{sum_of_Berns} we get that
\begin{align}\label{eq:EA_concentration}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sum\limits_{x,y\in A'}\1{x\sim y}\le cN\right)\quad&\le\quad \exp\left(-(1-\log2)c N\right).
\end{align}

Now let us turn to bounding the number of partitions with $|S|\le \varepsilon N$ and $\sum_{u\in U,\:v\in U^c}\1{u\sim v}\le\varepsilon N$.

For each $U\subseteq W$ let us define a corresponding $\widehat{U}\subseteq W$ such that $u\in \widehat{U}$ if and only if $u\in U$, $u+e_1\in U^c$ or $u\in U^c$, $u+e_1\in U$ (where $+e_1$ means increasing the first coordinate by one mod $\frac{n}{2}$). Then each $\widehat{U}\subseteq W$ corresponds to at most $2^{n^{d-1}}$ different choices of $U$.\footnote{More precisely each $\widehat{U}\subseteq W$ with an even number of elements in each `row' of the form $\{k\}\times\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{d-1}$ corresponds to exactly $2^{n^{d-1}}$ different choices of $U$.} Also, if $\sum_{u\in U,\:v\in U^c}\1{u\sim v}\le \varepsilon N$ then $|\widehat{U}|\le\varepsilon N$.

Therefore the number of pairs $(S,U)$ with $|S|\le \varepsilon N$, $\sum_{u\in U,\:v\in U^c}\1{u\sim v}\le \varepsilon N$ can be bounded as
\begin{align*}
&\le\quad2^{n^{d-1}}\left(\sum_{m=0}^{\varepsilon N}\binom{N/2}{m}\right)^2\quad\lesssim\quad 2^{n^{d-1}}\left(\varepsilon N\:\binom{N/2}{\varepsilon N}\right)^2 \quad\lesssim\quad 2^{n^{d-1}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon N}}{(2\varepsilon)^{\varepsilon N}(1-2\varepsilon)^{N/2-\varepsilon N}}\right)^2\quad\\
&\lesssim\quad\exp\left(N^{\frac{d-1}{d}}(\log 2)+ N\left(2\varepsilon\log\left(\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\right)+(1-2\varepsilon)\log\left(\frac{1}{1-2\varepsilon}\right)\right)+\log(\varepsilon N)\right).
\end{align*}

We have $2\varepsilon\log\left(\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\right)+(1-2\varepsilon)\log\left(\frac{1}{1-2\varepsilon}\right)\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, so by choosing $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small we can make the right-hand side $\lesssim\exp\left(\frac12(1-\log 2)cN\right)$. Then using \eqref{eq:EA_concentration} and taking a union bound finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{sum_of_Berns}
$ $\\
Let $S=\sum_{i=1}^{k}X_i$, where $X_i\sim\mathrm{Bern}\!\left(p_i\right)$ are independent, and let $\mu=\mathbb{E}\!\left[S\right]$.\\
Then for any $t>\mu$ we have
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(S\ge t\right)\le e^{-\mu}\left(\frac{e\mu}{t}\right)^t,
\]
and for any $t<\mu$ we have
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(S\le t\right)\le e^{-\mu}\left(\frac{e\mu}{t}\right)^t.
\]
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{sum_indep_RVs}
$ $\\
Let $S=\sum_{i=1}^{k}X_i$, where $X_i$ are independent, taking values in $[0,1]$, and let $\mu=\mathbb{E}\!\left[S\right]$. Then
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(S\ge \mu+t\right)\le& \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(\mu+t/3)}\right)&\forall t>0,\\
\mathbb{P}\!\left(S\le \mu-t\right)\le& \exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(\mu-t/3)}\right)&\forall t\in(0,\mu),\\
\mathbb{P}\!\left(S\ge c\mu\right)\le& \exp\left(-\mu\left(c\log\left(\frac{c}{e}\right)+1\right)\right)&\forall c>1.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{Bin_rough_tail_bound}
For any $M\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}$, $t\in\{0,1,...,M\}$, and $q\in(0,1)$ we have
\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\mathrm{Bin}\!\left(M,1-q\right)<t\right)\quad\le\quad M^tq^{M-t}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(\mathrm{Bin}\!\left(M,1-q\right)<t\right)\:=\:\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\binom{M}{s}(1-q)^{s}q^{M-s}\:\le\:\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}M^{s}q^{M-s}\:=\: q^M\frac{(Mq^{-1})^t-1}{Mq^{-1}-1}\:\le\: M^{t}q^{M-t}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
\label{Hb_properties}
Let $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$ and let $(p_i)$, $(q_i)$ and $(r_i)$ be sequences of real numbers taking values in $[0,\theta]$ where $\theta\in(0,1)$ is a sufficiently small constant (depending on $b$). Let $W$ be a random variable taking values in a countable set $\mathcal{W}$ {of size larger than some constant depending on $b$}. Then the following properties are satisfied.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item\label{property:decreasing}
If $p_i\ge q_i$ for all $i$, then
\[
H_{b}\left(p_1,p_2,...\right)\quad\ge\quad H_{b}\left(q_1,q_2,...\right).
\]
\item\label{property:splitting}
If $p_i=q_i+r_i$ for all $i$ then
\[
H_{b}\left(p_1,p_2,...\right)\quad\le\quad H_{b}\left(q_1,q_2,...\right)+H_{b}\left(r_1,r_2,...\right).
\]
\item\label{property:factorising}
If $p_i=q_ir_i$ for all $i$ then
\[
H_{b}\left(p_1,p_2,...\right)\quad\le\quad H_{b}\left(q_1,q_2,...\right)+H_{b}\left(r_1,r_2,...\right).
\]
\item\label{property:bound_by_set_size}
\[
H_{b}\left(W\right)\quad\le\quad\left(\log|\mathcal{W}|\right)^b.
\]
\item\label{property:bound_by_set_size_two}
If $p_1+...+p_N=p<1$ and $p_i=0$ for $i>N$ then
\[
H_{b}\left(p_1,p_2,...\right)\quad\lesssim\quad p\left(\log N\right)^b+p(-\log p)^b.
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- lemma-43: body_md -->
\label{Hb_cond_properties}Let $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$ and let $W$ and $Z$ be random variables as in \Cref{def:Hb_conditional}. Then
\begin{align*}
H_{b}\left(W\midZ\right)\quad&\le\quad H_{b}\left(W\right)+O(1),\\
H_{b}\left(W\right)\quad&\lesssim\quad H_{b}\left(W\midZ\right)+H_{b}\left(Z\right).
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-43 -->
<!-- lemma-44: body_md -->
\label{HbA_cond_properties} Let $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$, let $W$ and $Z$ be random variables as in \Cref{def:Hb_conditional}, and let $A\subseteq B$ be events. Then the following are satisfied.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item\label{item:HbA_cond_i}
\begin{align*}
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\midZ\right)\quad&\le\quad H_{b}^{A}\left(W\right)+O(1),\\
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\right)\quad&\lesssim\quad H_{b}^{A}\left(W\midZ\right)+H_{b}^{A}\left(Z\right).
\end{align*}
\item\label{item:HbA_cond_ii}
\begin{align*}
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\right)\quad&\le\quadH_{b}^{B}\left(W\right)+O(1),\\
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\midZ\right)\quad&\le\quadH_{b}^{B}\left(W\midZ\right)+O(1).
\end{align*}
\item\label{item:HbA_cond_iii} For each $z\in\mathcal{Z}$ let $\mathcal{W}_z=\{w:\:\mathbb{P}\left(W=w\;\middle\vert\;Z=z\right){}>0\}$. Then we have
\begin{align*}
H_{b}^{A}\left(W\midZ\right)\quad\lesssim\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\log|\mathcal{W}_Z|\right)^b\1{A}\right]+\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{P}\left(A\;\middle\vert\;Z\right){}\left(-\log\mathbb{P}\left(A\;\middle\vert\;Z\right){}\right)^b\right].
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-44 -->
<!-- lemma-45: body_md -->
\label{blue_almost_unif}
Let $(a_v)_{v\in V}$ be a collection of random variables that is distributed as the collection of blue degrees $d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)$ in $G^*$. Given $(a_v)_{v\in V}$, let $H_{(a_v)}$ be a random graph that can be obtained by adding $a_v$ blue half-edges to each vertex of the torus $G$ and then matching the blue half-edges uniformly randomly. Let $G_{(a_v)}$ be a random graph that is distributed like $G_b$ conditional on $\left\{d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)=a_v\:\forall v\in V\right\}$.

Then the graph $H_{(a_v)}$ conditioned on not having any loops or double edges has the same distribution as the graph $G_{(a_v)}$. Also, on the event
\begin{align*}
A:=\left\{\sum_{v}a_v\ge\frac{N}{C\log N},\:\sum_{v}a_v(a_v-1)\le\frac{CN}{(\log N)^{\frac32}},\:\sum_{u,v:u\ne v}a_v(a_v-1)a_u(a_u-1)\le\frac{CN^2}{(\log N)^3}\right\}.
\end{align*}
the probability of $H_{(a_v)}$ not having loops or double edges is $\ge1-\frac{C'}{(\log N)^{\frac12}}$ where $C'$ is a constant depending on $C$. Finally, for sufficiently large values of the constant $C$, we have $\mathbb{P}\!\left(A\right)=1-o(1)$.
<!-- end lemma-45 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The first part of the statement follows by noting that the probability of a given realisation of $G_{\mathrm{b}}$ only depends on the number of its blue edges, and that for a given sequence $(a_v)$, all configurations of $H_{(a_v)}$ without loops and double edges have the same probability.

Given the sequence $(a_v)$, the probability of $H_{(a_v)}$ having a loop is $\lesssim\sum_{v}\frac{a_v(a_v-1)}{(\sum_{x}a_x)-1}$ and the probability of $H_{(a_v)}$ having a double edge is $\lesssim\sum_{u,v:u\ne v}\frac{a_v(a_v-1)a_u(a_u-1)}{\left((\sum_{x}a_x)-1\right)^2}$. On the event $A$ these sums are both $\lesssim\frac{1}{(\log N)^{\frac12}}$ as required.

Finally, note that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{v}a_v(a_v-1)\right]\asymp\sum_x\sum_{y,z:\:y\ne z}\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} y,x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} z\right)\asymp N^3(p^{\mathrm{blue}})^2\asymp\frac{N}{(\log N)^2}$ and\\ 
$\sum_{u,v:u\ne v}a_v(a_v-1)a_u(a_u-1)\lesssim\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{v}a_v(a_v-1)\right]^2+\sum_{u,v:u\ne v}\mathbb{P}\!\left(u\sim_{\mathrm{b}} v\right)\mathbb{E}\!\left[a_v(a_v+1)\right]^2\lesssim\frac{N^2}{(\log N)^4}$. Using these and \Cref{total_blue_degree} we get that $\mathbb{P}\!\left(A\right)=1-o(1)$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-46: body_md -->
\label{degree_exp_moment}
For any $\theta\in\left[0,\frac14\right]$ we have $\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\thetad_{\mathrm{rgb}}}\right]\le e^{2\theta}$.
<!-- end lemma-46 -->
<!-- lemma-47: body_md -->
\label{volume_exp_moment}
Let $v$ be a fixed vertex and let $B_r$ denote the ball of radius $r$ around $v$ in $G^*$.\\
Then for any $\theta\in\left[0,\frac14\frac{1}{(2d+2)^r}\right]$ we have
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta\left|B_r\setminus B_{r-1}\right|}\right]\quad\le\quad e^{(2d+2)^r\theta},\]
and for any $\theta\in\left[0,\frac14\frac{1}{(2d+3)^r}\right]$ we have
\[\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta\left|B_r\right|}\right]\quad\le\quad e^{(2d+3)^r\theta}.\]

Furthermore, the same bounds hold if we consider a ball $B_r$ of radius $r$ around the root of a random quasi-tree $T$.
<!-- end lemma-47 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Note that
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\thetad_{\mathrm{rgb}}}\right]\quad=\quad\prod_{v}\left(p_{0,v}e^\theta+(1-p_{0,v})\right)\quad=\quad \prod_{v}\left(1+(e^\theta-1)p_{0,v}\right)\\
&=\quad\exp\left(\sum_{v}\log\left(1+(e^\theta-1)p_{0,v}\right)\right)\quad\le\quad \exp\left(\sum_{v}(e^\theta-1)p_{0,v}\right)\quad=\quad\exp\left(e^\theta-1\right),
\end{align*}
where we used the independence of edges and for the $\le$ we used that for any $x\ge0$ we have $\log(1+x)\le x$.

For $\theta\in\left[0,\frac14\right]$ we have $e^\theta-1\le2\theta$ which finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Note that both for balls in $G^*$ and for balls around the root of $T$ we have $\left(\left|B_r\setminus B_{r-1}\right|\right)_{r\ge1}\le_{\mathrm{st}}(Z_r)_{r\ge1}$ where $Z_r$ denotes the population size of generation $r$ of a Galton-Watson process with offspring distribution $\zeta\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}2d+d_{\mathrm{rgb}}$.

We prove by induction on $r$ that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta Z_r}\right]\le e^{(2d+2)^r\theta}$ for all $\theta\in\left[0,\frac14\frac{1}{(2d+2)^r}\right]$. For $r=0$ the statement is immediate.

Given the statement for $r=k$, and using \Cref{degree_exp_moment}, we can write
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta Z_{k+1}}\;\middle\vert\;Z_k\right]\quad=\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta\zeta}\right]^{Z_k}\quad=\quad\left(e^{2d\theta}\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\thetad_{\mathrm{rgb}}}\right]\right)^{Z_k}\quad\le\quad e^{(2d\theta+2\theta)Z_k},
\end{align*}
hence
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta Z_{k+1}}\right]\quad\le\quad\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\theta(2d+2)Z_k}\right]\quad\le\quad e^{(2d+2)^{k+1}\theta}
\end{align*}
as required.

The second part of the lemma can be proved analogously by noting that $\left(\left|B_r\right|\right)_{r\ge1}\le_{\mathrm{st}}(Z_r)_{r\ge1}$ where $Z_r$ denotes the population size of generation $r$ of a Galton-Watson process with offspring distribution $\zeta\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}2d+1+d_{\mathrm{rgb}}$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Using that $\left(\1{x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} y}\right)_{x,y\in V,\: x\ne y}$ are independent $\mathrm{Bern}\!\left(\frac{c_{\mathrm{b}}}{N\log N}\right)$ random variables, and the concentration bound \Cref{sum_of_Berns}, we get that whp $\left(1-\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}\le \sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\le\left(1+\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$.

This implies the required upper bound on $|\mathcal{A}|$. To facilitate the lower bounds on $|\mathcal{A}_C|$ and $|\mathcal{A}_x|$, we first prove that whp $|\mathcal{A}|\ge\left(1-\frac34\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$.

Note that conditional on $\sum_{v}d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)=S$, the distribution of the blue degrees can be obtained by choosing $\frac12S$ distinct pairs $\{x,y\}$ uniformly randomly and counting how many times each vertex appears. If $S\ge\left(1-\frac14\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}=:S_0$, then this stochastically dominates the numbers obtained by choosing $\frac12S_0$ distinct pairs $\{x,y\}$ uniformly randomly and counting the number of appearances of each vertex.

Let us consider choosing $\frac12S_0$ distinct pairs $\{x,y\}$ one by one, always choosing uniformly from the yet unchosen pairs. At each step, the probability of choosing a pair that contains a vertex that already appeared earlier is $\le\frac{S_0N}{\frac12N(N-1)-\frac12S_0}\asymp\frac{1}{\log N}$. Then using \Cref{sum_of_Berns} we get that whp there are $\lesssim \frac{N}{(\log N)^2}\le\frac18\theta c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$ pairs containing a vertex that already appeared earlier.

Putting these together, we get that whp the number of vertices with $d_{\mathrm{b}}\ge1$ is $\ge\left(1-\frac12\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$.

From \Cref{prob_nice} whp $\#\left\{v:\:d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\ge1,\:v\not\inV_{\mathrm{nice}}\right\}\le \frac{N}{(\log N)^{4/3}}\le\frac14\theta c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$. This finishes the proof of the lower bound on $|\mathcal{A}|$.

To bound the size of $\mathcal{A}_C$, we note that the green and red degrees of the vertices of $G^*$ can be stochastically dominated as follows. Let us consider a random directed graph $G_{\mathrm{rg}}^{(2)}$ where for each pair $(x,y)$ in $V$ there is a red directed edge from $x$ to $y$ with probability $p^{\mathrm{red}}_{x,y}$, and there is a green directed edge with probability $p^{\mathrm{green}}_{x,y}$, independently. Then we have
\[
\left(\deg^{(\mathrm{out})}(v)+\deg^{(\mathrm{in})}(v)\right)_{v\in V}\quad \ge_{\mathrm{st}}\quad\left(d_{\mathrm{rg}}(v)\right)_{v\in V},
\]
and $\deg^{(\mathrm{out})}(v)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}d_{\mathrm{rg}}$ are iid, and $\deg^{(\mathrm{in})}(v)\stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=}d_{\mathrm{rg}}$ are iid, but the outdegrees are not independent of the indegrees.

For any $v$ we have $\mathbb{P}\!\left(d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\ge2\right)\ll\frac{1}{\log N}$, hence whp $\#\left\{v:\:d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\ge2\right\}\le\frac18\thetac_{\mathrm{b}}\frac{N}{\log N}$. Conditioning on the blue edges, working on the high probability event that the number of vertices with $d_{\mathrm{b}}\ge1$ is $\ge\left(1-\frac34\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$ and $\le (1+\theta)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$, and using the above domination, we get that for any~$\theta$ for sufficiently large values of $C$ whp we have $\#\left\{v:d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\ge1 \text{ and }\deg(v)\ge C\right\}\le\frac{1}{16}\theta c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$. Therefore, $\#\left\{v\in \mathcal{A}:d_{\mathrm{b}}(v)\ge 2 \text{ or }\deg(v)\ge C \text{ or } (v'\sim_{\mathrm{b}} v\text{ and } \deg(v')\ge C )\right\}\le\frac24\theta c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$.\\ As whp $\left(1-\frac34\theta\right)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}\le|\mathcal{A}|\le(1+\theta)c_b\frac{N}{\log N}$ this finishes the proof of the lower bound on $|\mathcal{A}_C|$.

From \Cref{volume_high_prob_bound} we know that whp $G_{\mathrm{rg}}$ is such that for each vertex $x$ the number of vertices in its $2K$-neighbourhood is $\ll\frac{N}{\log N}$. This finishes the proof of the lower bound on $|\mathcal{A}_x|$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-48: body_md -->
\label{cond_green_red_deg}
There exists a positive constant $c$ with the following properties. For any $x,y\in V$, any $W\subseteq V\setminus\{x,y\}$ with $|W|\le N^{c}$, and any $k\ll\log N$ we have
\begin{align}\label{eq:simg_cond_prob}
\mathbb{P}\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{g}} y\;\middle\vert\;d_{\mathrm{g}}(y)=k,\:y\not\sim_{\mathrm{g}} w\:\:\:\forall w\in W\right){}\quad\asymp\quad k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{g}} y\right).
\end{align}
Furthermore, for any $x,y\in V$, any $W\subseteq V\setminus\{x,y\}$ with $|W|\le N^{1-\beta+c}$, and any $k\ll N^{1-\beta}\log N$ we have
\begin{align}\label{eq:simr_cond_prob}
\mathbb{P}\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{r}} y\;\middle\vert\;d_{\mathrm{r}}(y)=k,\:y\not\sim_{\mathrm{r}} w\:\:\:\forall w\in W\right){}\quad\asymp\quad k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{r}} y\right),
\end{align}
and for any $x,y\in V$, any $W\subseteq V\setminus\{x,y\}$ with $|W|\le cN$, and any $k\ll N$ we have
\begin{align}\label{eq:simb_cond_prob}
\mathbb{P}\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} y\;\middle\vert\;d_{\mathrm{b}}(y)=k,\:y\not\sim_{\mathrm{b}} w\:\:\:\forall w\in W\right){}\quad\asymp\quad 
k\cdot(\log N)\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim_{\mathrm{b}} y\right).
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-48 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
We present the proof \eqref{eq:simg_cond_prob}. {The proof of \eqref{eq:simr_cond_prob} is analogous, while \eqref{eq:simb_cond_prob} can be proved analogously or by direct computation of the two sides.}

	 
We assume that $|x-y|<D^{1-\beta}$ as otherwise the result is immediate. In the proof, we only consider green edges, so to simplify notation we drop the $g$ subscripts from $\sim_{\mathrm{g}}$ and $d_{\mathrm{g}}$. For a set $A\subseteq V$, let us write $d^A(y)=\sum_{z\in A}\1{z\sim y}$, $d^{-A}(y)=d^{V\setminus A}(y)$, and $d^{-A-x}(y)=d^{-(A\cup\{x\})}(y)$.

Note that \eqref{eq:simg_cond_prob} is equivalent to each of the following.
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim y,\:d(y)=k,\:y\not\sim w\:\forall w\in W\right)\quad&\asymp
\quad k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim y\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(d(y)=k,\:y\not\sim w\:\forall w\in W\right),\\
\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim y\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(y\not\sim w\:\forall w\in W\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k-1\right)\:&\asymp
\:k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim y\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(y\not\sim w\:\forall w\in W\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W}(y)=k\right),\\
\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k-1\right)\quad&\asymp\quad k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W}(y)=k\right).
\end{align*}
Note that
\begin{align*}
k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W}(y)=k\right)\quad=\quad k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim y\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k-1\right)+ k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\not\sim y\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k\right).
\end{align*}
We know that $k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\sim y\right)\lesssim\frac{k}{\log N}\ll1$, while $\mathbb{P}\!\left(x\not\sim y\right)\asymp1$, hence \eqref{eq:simg_cond_prob} is equivalent to
\begin{align}\label{eq:deg_eq_k}
\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k-1\right)\quad\asymp\quad k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k\right).
\end{align}
We can prove \eqref{eq:deg_eq_k} as follows. Note that we have
\begin{align*}
&k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k\right)\quad\\
&=\quad\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq(W\cup\{x,y\})^c\\|U|=k-1}}\sum_{z\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y\})^c}\left(\prod_{u\in U}\mathbb{P}\!\left(u\sim y\right)\right)\mathbb{P}\!\left(z\sim y\right)\left(\prod_{w\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y,z\})^c}\mathbb{P}\!\left(w\not\sim y\right)\right)\\
&=\quad\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq(W\cup\{x,y\})^c\\|U|=k-1}}\left(\prod_{u\in U}\mathbb{P}\!\left(u\sim y\right)\right)\left(\prod_{w\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y\})^c}\mathbb{P}\!\left(w\not\sim y\right)\right) \sum_{z\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y\})^c}\frac{\mathbb{P}\!\left(z\sim y\right)}{\mathbb{P}\!\left(z\not\sim y\right)}.
\end{align*}
For any given $U$, we have
\[
\sum\limits_{z\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y\})^c}\frac{\mathbb{P}\!\left(z\sim y\right)}{\mathbb{P}\!\left(z\not\sim y\right)}\quad\asymp\quad\sum\limits_{z\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y\})^c}\mathbb{P}\!\left(z\sim y\right)\quad=\quad \mathbb{E}\!\left[d(y)\right]-\mathbb{E}\!\left[d^{U\cup W\cup\{x\}}(y)\right],
\]
which is $\asymp1$, since we know that $\mathbb{E}\!\left[d(y)\right]\asymp1$, while $\mathbb{E}\!\left[d^{U\cup W\cup\{x\}}(y)\right]\lesssim\frac{\log|U\cup W\cup\{x\}|}{\log N}$ can be made arbitrarily small by choosing the constant $c$ in the bound $|W|\le N^c$ sufficiently small.

This shows that
\begin{align*}
&k\cdot\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W-x}(y)=k\right)\quad\\
&\asymp\quad\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq(W\cup\{x,y\})^c\\|U|=k-1}}\left(\prod_{u\in U}\mathbb{P}\!\left(u\sim y\right)\right)\left(\prod_{w\in(U\cup W\cup\{x,y\})^c}\mathbb{P}\!\left(w\not\sim y\right)\right)
\quad=\quad\mathbb{P}\!\left(d^{-W}(y)=k-1\right),
\end{align*}
which finishes the proof of \eqref{eq:deg_eq_k}, and hence the proof of \eqref{eq:simg_cond_prob}.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-49: body_md -->
\label{unit_flow_in_box}
There exists a constant $C$ with the following property. For any $d\ge3$, any $r$, and any two vertices $x$ and $y$ in a box $[0,r]^d$ (with edges induced by $\mathbb{Z}^d$) there exists a unit flow $\theta$ from $x$ to $y$ in the box that has energy $\le C$.
<!-- end lemma-49 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
It is sufficient to prove the statement in the case $x=(0,...,0)$. (If $\theta_x$ is a unit flow $0\to x$ and $\theta_y$ is a unit flow $0\to y$, then $\theta_y-\theta_x$ is a unit flow $x\to y$ with energy $\le2\left(\mathcal{E}(\theta_x)+\mathcal{E}(\theta_y)\right)$.)

Let $z_0$, ..., $z_{d}$ be a sequence of vertices in the box such that $|z_0-x|_{\infty}\le1$, $z_{d}=y$, and for each $i\in\{1,2,...,d\}$ the vertices $z_{i-1}$ and $z_{i}$ are opposing corners of a $d$-dimensional cube within the box.

We can prove that such a sequence always exists by induction on $d$ as follows.

For $d=1$ the statement is true. Now let $d\ge2$ and assume that the statement is true for smaller dimensions. Wlog $y=(y_1,...,y_d)$ where $y_1\ge ...\ge y_d\ge0$. Let $r_d=\lfloor\frac{y_{d-1}-y_{d}}{2}\rfloor$ and let $z_{d-1}=y+(-r_d,...,-r_d,r_d)$. Note that in $z_{d-1}$ all coordinates are nonnegative, they are all $\le r$, and the last two coordinates differ by at most 1. Let $x_{d-1}$ agree with $x$ in the first $d-1$ coordinates and differ in the last coordinate by at most 1 such that in $z_{d-1}-x_{d-1}$ the last two coordinates agree. Now use the result for $d-1$ dimensions for $x_{d-1}$ and $z_{d-1}$, identifying the last two coordinates.\hfill //

From~\cite[Exercise 9.1]{MTMC} we know that for each $i$ there exists a unit flow $\theta_i$ in the box from $z_{i-1}$ to $z_i$, with energy bounded by an absolute constant $C'$. Also, there is a unit flow $\theta_0$ in the box from $x$ to $z_0$ with energy bounded by $d$. Then $\theta:=\sum_{i=0}^{d}\theta_i$ is a unit flow in the box from $x$ to $y$ with energy bounded by $(d+1)^2(C'\vee d)$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-50: body_md -->
\label{near_bipartiteness}
Let $P$ be the transition matrix of a reversible Markov chain on a state space $\Omega$ of size $n$, with stationary distribution $\pi$.
Let $1=\lambda_1\geq\lambda_2\geq\ldots\geq \lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of $P$, and let $f_i$ be the corresponding unit eigenfunctions, such that $P f_i=\lambda_i f_i$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\!\left[f_i f_j\right]=\1{i=j}$.
Then if $1+\lambda_n \leq c'\left(1-\lambda_2\right)$ for some absolute constant $c' \in (0,1) $ then
$\text{Var}_{\pi}\left|f_n\right| \leq \frac{1+\lambda_n}{1-\lambda_2}$.

Moreover, if we let
\[F_{+}:=\left\{x: f_n(x) \geq 0\right\}\quad \text { and }\quad F_{-}:=\left\{x: f_n(x)<0\right\}\]
then $\left|\pi\left(F_{+}\right)-1 / 2\right|=\left|\pi\left(F_{-}\right)-1 / 2 \right|\lesssim\frac{1+\lambda_n}{1-\lambda_2}$, and the parity breaking time defined by
\[S:=\quad\inf\left\{i:\left(X_{i-1}, X_i\right) \in (F_{+}\times F_{+}) \cup (F_{-}\times F_{-})\right\}\] satisfies for some $\beta>\left|\lambda_n\right|$ that for all $k$ we have
\[\left(1-\frac{2\left(1+\lambda_n\right)}{1-\lambda_2}\right)(\beta^{2k}+\beta^{2k+1})\quad\leq\quad \mathbb{P}_{\pi}\!\left(S>2k\right)+\mathbb{P}_{\pi}\!\left(S>2k+1\right)\quad\leq\quad (\beta^{2k}+\beta^{2k+1}).\]
<!-- end lemma-50 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
We apply \Cref{near_bipartiteness} to the simple random walk on $H$. We assume, for the sake of contradiction, that $\varepsilont_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\ge t_\mathrm{rel}$ for a constant $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ to be chosen later.
Since $F_+$ and $F_-$ form a partition of $V$, by the assumption of the proposition we have $|E(F_-)|+|E(F_+)|\ge c|E|$. As the first edge crossed by a random walk starting from an invariant distribution is a uniformly chosen edge of the graph, this means that $\mathbb{P}_{\pi}\!\left(S=1\right)\ge c$.

On the other hand, by \Cref{near_bipartiteness} we also have
\[\left(1-\frac{2\left(1+\lambda_n\right)}{1-\lambda_2}\right)(\beta^{2}+\beta^{3}) \quad\leq\quad \mathbb{P}_{\pi}\!\left(S>2\right)+\mathbb{P}_{\pi}\!\left(S>3\right)\quad\le\quad 2\mathbb{P}_{\pi}\!\left(S>1\right)\quad{\le}\quad 2(1-c).\]
We assumed that $\frac{2\left(1+\lambda_n\right)}{1-\lambda_2}\le2\frac{t_\mathrm{rel}}{t_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}}\le 2\varepsilon$, and we have that $\beta\ge |\lambda_n|\ge 1-\frac{\varepsilon}{t_\mathrm{rel}}\ge 1-\varepsilon$. Therefore,
\[(1-2\varepsilon)((1-\varepsilon)^2+(1-\varepsilon)^3)\quad\le\quad 2(1-c).\]
Choosing a sufficiently small constant value of $\varepsilon$ (in terms of $c$), this gives a contradiction. Therefore, we have $t_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\lesssim t_\mathrm{rel}$.
We know that $t_\mathrm{rel}^{\mathrm{abs}}\get_\mathrm{rel}$ always holds, so this completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
